MHBM001: LURASIDONE CAN RELIEVE THE PROLONGED QTC INTERVAL DURING TREATMENT: A CASE REPORT Cunbo Wu a , Kexiang Cheng a , Yuan Li a , Xiaolin Tan a a Chongqing Mental Health Center, Gele Mountain, Shapingba District, Chongqing, 400036, China. Background: As one of the second-generation new antipsychotics approved by the US FDA from 2009 to 2010, lurasidone does not affect QTc interphase and has little effect on metabolism, improve the cognitive function, so it is well received in clinical practice and has established a unique position in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. In patients with schizophrenia, taking other antipsychotics can lead to a prolonged QTc interval. At this point, lurasidone becomes the preferred choice for schizophrenia patients with prolonged QTc interval. Subjects and methods: A 75-year-old elderly woman with schizophrenia, such as soliloquy, nonsense, behavior disorder, suspected of being a victim, suspected of stealing, such that Emotional response is not coordinated, after admission to talk about their illness a straight face with a smile, talking about the death of their loved ones laughing, behavior disorder, at home disorderly water mop, lying in bed for a long time closed eyes, often kneeling on the ground to pray to God, there is yelling during night sleep, sometimes at home, pushing, scolding her husband, mumbling, repeatedly pouring water at home mopping the floor, washing hair with cold water many times a day without blowing, closing your eyes for a long time or kneeling on the ground to pray to God, etc., yelling occurs during sleep at night. etc., High risk for impulsivity, low risk for suicide. What’s worse, she developed electrocardiogram abnormalities (prolonged Qtc interval) in the course of treatment, stopped using psycho-related drugs for 1 week to wait for lurasidone to arrive, and then changed to lurasidone 40 mg/d antipsychotic treatment. Assisted with psychological treatment, behavior modification treatment, transcranial magnetic stimulation, brain electrical biofeedback treatment to promote the recovery of patients. Results: The patient’s ECG showed that QTc interval returned to normal. His mental symptoms improved and she was discharged, Gradually stable mood, get along well with patients, occasionally kneeling to worship Buddha behavior, general conditions can be, no physical discomfort.. Conclusion: Lurasidone is highly favored for its cognitive enhancement in the treatment of schizophrenia, not only does it not affect the QTc interphase and metabolism, but also relieves the QTc interval prolongation. MHBM002: META-ANALYSIS OF TREATING DIARRHEA IN SHEEP OR GOAT WITH TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE Jinxin Li a , Jia Min a , Yu Wang a , Zhiwei Guo a , Haijing Zhu a , Junjun Zhai a , Longping Li a , Lei Qu a , Shuwei Dong a a Shaanxi Province Engineering &amp; Technology Research Center of Shanbei Cashmere Goats, Yulin University, Yulin, Shaanxi, China. Background: In order to review systematically on the clinical efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine in the treatment of sheep diarrhea, the literature about clinical trials of treating diarrhea in sheep or goat were searched in Chinese and English database (CNKI, WanFang, VIP, CBMdisc, Web of Science, PubMed, and Embase) with the keywords of diarrhea, sheep or goat and traditional Chinese medicine. Subjects and Methods: 558 references were collected, and 12 clinical trials were finally screened after reading the title and abstract in EndNote X9. The basic information was extracted, and then Meta-analysis was carried out by Rev Manager (Version 5.4). 1351 cases, including 678 cases in the experimental group and 673 cases in the control group. The experimental group is treated with traditional Chinese medicine, and the control group is treated with modern Western medicine. Results: Meta-analysis results demonstrate that, in terms of cure rates, within the subgroup of literature published after 2010, the experimental group exhibits a superior cure rate compared to the control group [OR = 2.07, 95% CI (1.52, 2.83), p &lt; 0.01]. In the subgroup of literature published before 2010, the experimental group’s cure rate significantly outperforms the control group [OR = 28.31, 95% CI (10.68, 75.03), p &lt; 0.01]. The total cure rates for the experimental and control groups are 87.46% (593/678) and 67.16% (452/673), respectively, suggesting that traditional Chinese medicine’s overall cure rate for treating sheep diarrhea surpasses that of Western medicine [OR = 2.94, 95% CI (1.78, 4.85), p &lt; 0.01]. In terms of the overall effective rate, the experimental group’s rate surpasses that of the control group, at 89.77% (193/215) and 77.29% (160/207), respectively, indicating that traditional Chinese medicine’s overall effectiveness in treating sheep diarrhea is superior to Western medicine [OR = 2.57, 95% CI (1.48, 4.44), p &lt; 0.01]. Subgroup analysis based on the publication year of the literature reveals significant heterogeneity between literature published after 2010 and before 2010 (p &lt; 0.05, I2 &gt; 50%). Moreover, the 95% CI of the two groups’ effect sizes doesn’t overlap, indicating an interaction effect of the publication year on the effect values. Conclusions: Based on the present trial evidence, traditional Chinese medicine demonstrates superior clinical efficacy in treating sheep diarrhea compared to Western medicine. The result provides a valuable clinical decision-making guidance for treating sheep diarrhea in practical production and lays a foundation for future research and drug development for preventing and treating diarrhea. Acknowledgments This work was supported by the project grant from the High-Level Talent Research Start-up Project of Yulin University (18GK10), Collaborative Innovation Projects of Education Office of Shaanxi Province (22JY076), National Natural Science Regional Fund (31960710) and Natural Science Basic Research Program of Shaanxi (2022JM-102). MHBM003: ANALYSIS OF MARINE ECOLOGY AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH Aina Bao a , Hongbing Jiang a a Yantai Institute of Science and Technology, Yantai, 265600, China. Background: We analyzed the marine ecological security changes in Penglai District, and pointed its impact on public mental health. Then we gave ways to improve marine ecological and public mental health. Subjects and Methods: The AHP and the comprehensive index evaluation method are used to analyzed the Marine ecological environment changes, and questionnaire survey, observation method and case study method is used to analyze the change of public mental health. Results: This paper analyzed the circumstances and existing problems of marine ecological security in Penglai District. By establishing the influencing factors of marine ecological indicators, we constructed the marine ecological security index system and then clarified the evaluation method of the index system. Using the remote sensing data, the Shandong Marine Ecological Environment Bulletin, the Yantai City Statistical Annual Sign and the Penglai District National Economic and Social Development Statistical Bulletin, various indicators required for marine safety evaluation in Penglai District were extracted. The weight of each evaluation index is determined using the AHP and the comprehensive index evaluation method. Then the marine ecological safety level is determined. Also, we discussed the impact of changes in the Marine environment on public mental health, As the Marine ecology deteriorates, people may experience emotional states such as fear, anxiety and depression, which may further lead to an increase in the incidence of psychological disorders and mental illness. Therefore, it is necessary to improve the Marine ecological environment and improve public mental health. Finally, corresponding environmental protection countermeasures are formulated according to the evaluation results. Conclusions: Marine ecological environment is closely related to public mental health. A deteriorating Marine environment may trigger anxiety and restlessness, lower self-confidence, depression and sadness, and increase stress and burden. When the marine ecological environment is improved, people are able to enjoy a better time at the seaside, which helps to reduce stress and thus improve mental health. In addition, the improved Marine environment also helps to enhance people’s sense of awe and closeness to the natural environment. When people realize that their actions can affect the Marine environment, they will be more willing to participate in actions to protect the environment. This sense of engagement and achievement can increase self-esteem and self-confidence, which can have a positive impact on mental health. Acknowledgments This research is supported by the Ministry of Education Production and education cooperation project (220602070274703) and the Yantai Philosophy and Social Science Rules Project (2020YTSK-100). MHBM004: SURGICAL AND CAPECITABINE INTERVENTION FOR LOCALLY RECURRENT MALIGNANT PHYLLODES TUMOR OF THE BREAST: CASE REPORT AND LITERATURE REVIEW Chengpeng Zhao a , Chengxing Wu b , Xingyue Zhang c , Peng Zhao d , Tongxian Huo e , Shaoce Xu f , Yan Wang d a Department of Breast surgery, Qinghai Province Cancer Hospital, Sining 810000, China, b Department of General surgery, The People’s Hospital of Pubei, Qinzhou 535300, China, c Clinical College, Qilu Medical University, Linyi 255300, China, d Department of Breast surgery, Third People’s Hospital of Gansu Province, Lanzhou 730030, China, e Third People’s Hospital of Gansu Province, Lanzhou 730030, China, f Department of Pathology, Lanzhou University Second Hospital, Lanzhou 730030, China. CZ and CW contributed equally to this study. Background: This study aspires to provide an in-depth examination of a complex medical case involving a locally recurrent giant malignant lobulated breast tumor. The primary focus is to unravel the intricacies associated with its heightened recurrence rate and resistance to traditional treatments, such as chemotherapy and targeted therapy. The overarching goal is to meticulously analyze the effectiveness of a holistic therapeutic approach that encompasses chemoembolization, surgery, and postoperative capecitabine chemotherapy in achieving complete remission. Subjects and Methods: The case in question revolves around a patient grappling with a recurrent malignant phyllodes tumor of the breast, persisting despite prior rounds of chemotherapy and targeted therapy. To confront this challenging scenario head-on, chemoembolization was administered to precisely target the tumor’s vascularity, followed by surgical intervention for the meticulous excision of the recurrent tumor. Subsequently, the patient underwent a carefully monitored course of postoperative capecitabine chemotherapy. The multidisciplinary nature of this treatment approach is highlighted, emphasizing the collaborative efforts of oncologists, surgeons, and a spectrum of healthcare professionals. Results: The patient exhibited a remarkably favorable response to the amalgamated therapeutic strategy, achieving complete remission subsequent to the implementation of chemoembolization, surgery, and capecitabine chemotherapy. This successful outcome serves as a compelling testament to the potential efficacy ingrained in a multidisciplinary approach when managing locally recurrent malignant phyllodes tumors of the breast. The case accentuates the critical imperative of exploring alternative treatment modalities in the face of tumors resistant to conventional therapies. Conclusions: Our findings underscore the paramount importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in the triumphant management of locally recurrent malignant phyllodes tumors. The strategic integration of chemoembolization, surgery, and capecitabine chemotherapy has proven not only highly effective but also holds promise as a valuable treatment option for cases refractory to conventional therapies. Moreover, the comprehensive literature review embedded in this study offers insightful guidance for clinicians, underscoring the need for a thorough understanding of available treatment modalities to optimize patient outcomes in challenging cases of malignant phyllodes tumors of the breast. In conclusion, the multifaceted therapeutic approach outlined in this case study not only contributes to the evolving landscape of breast tumor management but also holds promise for the advancement of clinical strategies in dealing with such intricate malignancies. Acknowledgments We would like to convey our sincere deep-felt gratitude to the geriatric patient for consenting and permission granted to publish this work. Also, we would like to acknowledge all team members and the multidisciplinary team for the discussions, verifications and approval of our work up plan for this patient. This work was supported by the Gansu Provincial Health Industry Research Program (GSWSKY2022-40). At present, Ningde has comprehensively conquered absolute poverty. In the post-poverty alleviation era, the city should focus on consolidating and improving the results of poverty alleviation, realize the effective connection between poverty management and rural revitalization, and prevent the occurrence of systemic and regional large-scale return to poverty. MHBM006: CLINICAL EFFICACY OF INTEGRATED TRADITIONAL CHINESE AND WESTERN MEDICINE IN THE TREATMENT OF ANKYLOSING SPONDYLITIS: A META-ANALYSIS Li Deng a , Siyu Tao b , Yuqi Tang a , Tao Xiang a , Long Jia a , Ming Cheng a a JinNiu District Pepple’s Hospital of Chengdu,Chengdu 610036,China, b College of acupuncture and massage, Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Chengdu Sichuan Province, 610075, China. LD and ST contributed equally to this work. Background: Integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine (iTCWM) is widely used in clinical practice, but its effectiveness in the treatment of ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is still controversial. Given this, this study uses evidence-based medicine to analyze and evaluate the efficacy and safety of iTCWM for AS. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science and Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and WangFang Data were searched for relevant literature on iTCWM in the treatment of AS. Meta-analysis was then performed using Stata16.0 software. Results: A total of 603 relevant articles were retrieved and 15 studies were finally included. Compared with Western medicine alone, iTCWM led to a higher effective rate (OR = 4.35, 95% CI: 3.18, 5.95) and a lower incidence of adverse reactions (OR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.25, 0.81). Additionally, C-reactive protein (CRP) level (SMD = -1.26, 95% CI: -1.66, -0.87), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR, SMD = -1.53, 95% CI: -2.10, -0.95), and Bath ankylosing spondylitis disease activity index (BASDAI) (SMD = -1.41, 95% CI: -2.11, -0.71) after iTCWM treatment were lower than after Western medicine alone. The combined therapy also significantly shorten the duration of morning stiffness (SMD = -1.08, 95% CI: -2.13, -0.03) in AS patients. Conclusion: In the treatment of AS, iTCWM leads to a better prognosis and can effectively improve the biochemical indicators and physiological response of patients, which is worthy of clinical application. MHBM007: ANALYSIS OF COVID-19 GOVERNMENT RESPONSE STRINGENCY INDEX AND NATIONAL MENTAL HEALTH IMPACT BASED ON LSTM MODEL Lihe Ma a , Wenjing Lu a a School of Information Engineering, Harbin University, Harbin, China. Background: To divide the 170000 COVID-19 cases opened on a platform into developed countries, developing countries, and least developed countries according to the World Bank’s criteria for dividing economic development into developed countries, developing countries, and least developed countries based on the authoritative data set related to Government Response Stringency Index and national mental health impact, To analyze the relationship between the Government Response Stringency Index adopted by various countries and the impact on the mental health of the population during the COVID-19 pandemic. Subjects and Methods: In this study, the long and short term memory (LSTM) model was used to analyze the relationship between the Government Response Stringency Index for COVID-19 and the impact of national mental health. The LSTM model is a recursive neural network that can capture long-term dependencies in time series data, making it suitable for analyzing the dynamic nature of the epidemic and its impact on mental health. The data set contains the daily data of the Government Response Stringency Index adopted by the countries to deal with COVID-19, including basic medical conditions, the number of new cases per day, the number of new cases per day and other information. In addition, it includes data on national mental health indicators such as depression, anxiety, and stress. Divide the dataset into training, testing, and validation sets, and use these data to train, test, and validate the LSTM model. Results: The research results indicate that in developed countries, due to their good economic level and strong medical foundation, the Government Response Stringency Index was very high in the early stages of the epidemic, reaching the highest level in the Delta era. By the Omicron era, the mortality rate had decreased to a very low level. At the same time, with the popularization of vaccines and the introduction of specific drugs, the Government Response Stringency Index gradually decreased; People may have easier access to mental health services, including online counseling, psychotherapy, and medication. Due to limitations in economic development and healthcare infrastructure, the average Government Response Stringency Index in least developed countries is lower than that of developed countries; In many LDCs, the COVID-19 epidemic may bring greater pressure to the already fragile medical system, which may lead to the neglect of the diagnosis and treatment of mental health problems. The economic development level of developing countries is average, and the basic medical conditions are poor, which is between developed and least developed countries; The availability of mental health services may be limited, especially in rural and remote areas. The epidemic may exacerbate the existing resource shortages in these areas. Conclusions: There is a significant correlation between the Government Response Stringency Index of COVID-19 and the impact of national mental health. Research has shown that countries implementing stricter government response measures often encounter higher levels of mental health problems among their populations. This indicates that strict measures such as blockades and travel restrictions may have unexpected effects on individuals’ mental health. In addition, the impact of mental health is not only determined by the severity of government measures, but also by other background factors such as access to mental health resources, social support systems, and socio-economic conditions. These findings highlight the multifaceted nature of the relationship between government response measures and mental health outcomes. MHBM008: A REVIEW OF FIVE-ELEMENT MUSIC THERAPY FOR THE TREATMENT OF DIFFERENT DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS: PRINCIPLES, METHODS AND ANALYSIS Jingru Liu a , Wen Qin b , Ying Du a , Wendi Fu a a Chinese Medicine Cultural Research and Dissemination Centre, Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, Harbin, China, b Key Laboratory of Basic and Application Research of Beiyao (Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine), Ministry of Education, School of Pharmacy, Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, Harbin, China Background: At present, there are limitations in the treatment of depression in the world, and each patient’s depressive symptoms are different. Therefore, more targeted and effective methods are needed to solve this problem. Subjects and Methods: In order to find more targeted treatment methods, through the search of CNKI database and PubMed database, through the search of depression phase and treatment methods related keywords, we found a very suitable method, five elements music therapy. Results: Through a query in the existing database, multiple evidence shows that: five-element music therapy is targeted to treat different symptoms of depression according to different tunes. Gong tune music is mainly aimed at patients with depression and prominent digestive symptoms. Shang tune music is mainly aimed at patients with obvious respiratory symptoms of depression. Jue tune music is viewed as a treatment for depression, which concludes irritability, panic and flank pain. Zhi tune music is mainly aimed at patients with obvious cardiovascular symptoms of depression. Yu tune music is targeted at patients with significant reproductive system symptoms of depression. Conclusions: Five-element music has a exceeding effect on the clinical treatment of depression symptoms, and there is also very clear evidence for the improvement of related depression indicators in the treatment process. MHBM010: THE CORRELATION BETWEEN CYTOKINES IN AQUEOUS HUMOR AND BLOOD TEST INDICATORS IN PATIENTS WITH PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY COMPLICATED BY MACULAR EDEMA Enliang Ding a , Enguang Ding a , Dan Meng a , Yongli Li a , Hongyu Su a a HanDan AiYan Ophthalmology Hospital, Handan Hebei 056008, China Background: This study aims to investigate the correlation between various cytokine levels in the aqueous humor and blood test indices in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) complicated by macular edema (ME). Methods: Twenty-eight eyes of 28 patients diagnosed with PDR and ME were retrospectively selected from HanDan AiYan Ophthalmology Hospital between October 2019 and May 2023. According to the morphological characteristics observed in optical coherence tomography (OCT), the patients were categorized into two groups: those with cystoid macular edema (CME type, 12 cases, 12 eyes) and those with serous retinal detachment (SRD type, 16 cases, 16 eyes).The levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), growth factor (GF), and the inflammatory cytokines interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 were compared between the two groups. Additionally, the study compared the levels of glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fibrinogen (FIB), serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides(TG), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), platelet count (PLT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet crit (PCT), platelet distribution width (PDW), and bilirubin (Bil), as well as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Furthermore, the correlation between cytokines and blood test parameters in the aqueous humor was analyzed. Results: The IL-6 level was higher in the SRD group than in the CME group, and this difference was statistically significant (P&lt;0.05). The total cholesterol (TC) of the patients in the SRD group was lower than that in the CME group, and this difference was statistically significant (P&lt;0.05). The levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) in the aqueous humor of both groups, as well as the differences in blood test indexes, were not statistically significant (P&gt;0.05). The levels of VEGF were positively correlated with HbA1c (r=0.434, P&lt;0.05). IL-6 was positively correlated with IL-8 (r=0.695, P&lt;0.01) and negatively correlated with TC (r= -0.453, P&lt;0.05). IL-8 was negatively correlated with NEUT (r=-0.464, P&lt;0.05). There was no apparent correlation between Bil, FIB, NLR, HDL-C, LDL-C, and platelet count (P&gt;0.05). Conclusions: Patients with PDR and OCT exhibit higher levels of inflammatory factors compared to patients with CME. This suggests the necessity of anti-inflammatory treatment in patients with DR with SRD. The levels of VEGF levels in patients with PDR and ME show a moderate correlation with HbA1c levels. DR focuses on local treatment outcomes and educates patients about the importance of long-term effective blood glucose management. MHBM011: DUAL APPLICATION OF DISTRIBUTED BLOCK-CHAIN TECHNOLOGY IN MEDICAL HEALTHCARE AND DIGITAL ECONOMY Yue Xiao a , Shan Jiang a , Shu Liu a , Tianru Wang a , Yichen Cui a , Hongying Tian a a School of Economic Management, Wuhan Institute of Technology, Wuhan, China. Objective: To analyze the dual application of distributed block-chain technology in digital currency security risks, combining the needs of medical health field. Aiming to study and ensure the security, privacy, and traceability of medical information and health data of patients, providing a solid data foundation for further promoting the digital development of medical field. By enhancing the transparency and efficiency of data sharing, we can better serve personalized treatment and digitized health management for patients. Method: This study is based on distributed block-chain technology and explores its dual application in medical health data security and digital economy in depth. By establishing a decentralized data storage system, we ensure the security, privacy, and immutability of healthy economy data. Building a secure and tamper proof medical record system based on block-chain technology to prevent unauthorized access and tampering, ensuring the integrity and credibility of patient medical data. By establishing a secure data storage and sharing platform, utilizing smart contracts and encryption technology, using virtual currency, patients can control health data and track medical records, maximizing the protection of patient privacy. Using block-chain technology to establish trust between patients and medical teams, promoting more effective treatment processes, improving the quality of medical services, and providing innovative solutions for digital healthcare and development of health economy. Result: This study delved into the application of distributed block-chain technology in the health economy data management. Research has found that block-chain technology performs excellently in protecting patient privacy, enhancing data security and integrity. This technology can significantly reduce the risk of data leakage and misuse. Block-chain not only ensures the transparency and accuracy of data, but also helps improve the efficiency of diagnosis and treatment by ensuring data integrity. Block-chain technology can provide a secure and decentralized data storage and sharing platform when processing sensitive health data. Conclusion: In order to enhance the security and privacy protection of health economy data, achieve high efficiency and accuracy of data sharing, and promote interdisciplinary collaboration and the effectiveness of personalized treatment for patients, this article suggests the widespread application of distributed block-chain technology in the field of health economy. During this process, attention should be paid to ensuring data integrity and immutability, providing strong data access and control mechanisms, and reducing the risk of economic information leakage and misuse. At the same time, emphasis should be placed on the application of smart contracts to ensure automated and secure data processing. On the basis of ensuring data security and privacy, more effectively utilize medical and health data to provide better medical services and to promote the development of health economy. MHBM012: A SEMI-AUTOMATIC ANNOTATION SYSTEM FOR BUILDING A PSYCHOLOGICAL ANXIETY RELIEF-ORIENTED LEGAL KNOWLEDGE GRAPH Mingwei Tang a , Senshuai Zhao a , Yi Zhu a , Jing Chen b , Dong Zhang c a School of Computer, Nanjing Audit University, Nanjing City 210000, China, b Jiangsu United Creidt Co., LTD., Nanjing City 210000, China, c Nanjing Glaway Software Co., LTD., Nanjing City 210000, China Background: In the legal domain, legal know- ledge is important to not only law practitioners, but also ordinary beings. The rich legal knowledge may provide help for their lives. Knowledge graph is an efficient tool to express and offer knowledge in a specific domain. Therefore, in the legal domain, a high-quality knowledge graph, like an intelligent legal knowledge dictionary, could provide rich legal knowledge for the people involved in the judicial related events and then help relieve their psychological anxiety. Then how to build a legal knowledge graph? Despite recent advances in information extraction (IE) techniques, no suitable automated methods can be applied to constructing a domain-specific, comprehensive, and high-quality knowledge graph. However, a semi-automatic strategy, which can ensure the basic quality requirements of a knowledge graph, has been successfully implemented in the elementary science domain. The paper employs the idea to proposed a semi-automatic annotation system for building a legal knowledge graph. Subjects and Methods: This paper presents a semantic annotation system developed for building a high-quality legal knowledge graph using the semi-automatic strategy. We use a semi-automatic annotation method for extract the triples from legal texts. The method first uses NLP technology to recognize the entities from legal texts. Then annotate the relations of entities manually. Based on the method, we design the semi-automatic annotation system. The system’s architecture, algorithms, functions and implementation are presented in detail. To investigate the effectiveness of the system, we conduct a preliminary annotation experiment with 280 legal texts which were collected from the Harvard Caselaw Access Project. Results: The user evaluation from 32 graduate students demonstrates the high usability of the system in semantic annotation and the potential for building a high-quality legal knowledge graph. The contents in the knowledge graph shows the clear legal knowledge. It could provide legal aid for related individuals to relieve their psychological anxiety when they are involved in legal dispute. Conclusions: By the system, a high-quality legal knowledge graph could be built. That could be the foundation of building an intelligent system which could relieve psychological anxiety for the legal related individualsm, and can also be adapted to other fields for constructing domain-specific knowledge graphs. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a pervasive health condition that significantly reduces life expectancy by promoting myocardial infarction and ischemic heart disease. Even when patients with CAD receive optimal treatment, many continue to experience persistent angina pectoris (AP) and dyspnea. Research has indicated that some degree of symptom improvement may be attributed to placebo effects and environmental factors. Subjects and Methods: The study design was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial involving 144 patients with stable CAD who had undergone successful PCI. Results: The researchers expected a 10-point difference in the SAQ quality of life scores between the control and intervention groups (effect size d=0.5). The study required 64 patients per group, assuming an 80% test power. Considering a 10% dropout rate, 144 patients were recruited. Analyses were performed using covariance. Conclusions: The aim of our research is to utilize these observations and translate them into improved outcomes for stable CHD patients. This is especially essential as this pathology constitutes a very common, limited, and often difficult-to-treat condition. We performed an in-depth study of the effect of PCI and discussed the possibility of visual presentation in improving patient perception of treatment, enhancing confidence in treatment, and reducing anxiety. Our research does not exclude patients who have already had angiographic results shown in the catheterization room, as our goal is to evaluate the effect of this simple visual display. MHBM023: SIS MATHEMATICAL MODEL AND BASIC REPRODUCTIVE NUMBER OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES BASED ON PYTHON APPLICATION SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS Jie Liu a , Fan Yang b a College of Information, Wuhan Vocational College of Software and Engineering (Wuhan Open University), Wuhan, 430205, China, b College of Computer, Hubei University of Education, Wuhan, 430205, China. Objective: With the acceleration of the process of global integration, the threat posed by major outbreaks to human health and security and socio-economic development is growing. Almost every year, one or more emerging acute infectious diseases appear in the world. This paper is based on the SIS two state infectious disease model, that is, there are only two kinds of people, the susceptible people and the infected people. The infected people will turn into infected people after the infection recovers. Under this model, the basic reproduction number of this kind of infectious disease is solved and analyzed. Methods: There are many existing models about infectious diseases. In this study, we selected the SIS model, a common warehouse model, to solve the mathematical equation of the model, obtain its basic regeneration number, and use python programming to realize the program expression of the model, and then analyze the sensitivity of various key elements in the model. Results: The experimental results show that when the basic reproduction number is greater than 1, the epidemic of SIS model will break out or become popular, while when the basic reproduction number is less than or equal to 1, the epidemic will not break out or become popular. Infection rate and recovery rate have a great impact on the evolution of infectious disease events, and improving recovery rate is more significant in the prevention and control of disease transmission. Conclusions: This paper uses mathematical analysis and program analysis to solve and analyze the basic reproduction number of SIS infectious disease model. Compared with the reality, the model has certain practical significance. In the future, more practical factors can be considered for further research. MHBM032: TRANSLATION TERMINOLOGY, PSYCHOLOGICAL COGNITION AND MENTAL HEALTH: A CASE STUDY OF THE MONGOLIAN TRANSLATION OF “FILIAL PIETY”, “FRATERNAL DUTY”, “LOYALTY”, AND “WORRY” IN THE “CLASSIC OF FILIAL PIETY” Guojun Ren a , Shuaijie Qin b a Beijing Language and Culture University, Beijing, China (Postal code: 100083), b Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Beijing, China (Postal code: 100732 ) Background: Different ethnic groups often choose different words to express the same cultural concept. Investigating the differences in translation terminology for the same cultural concept is crucial for exploring the cultural psychological cognition of various ethnicities from the perspective of mental health. Subjects and Methods: This paper employs a comparative research approach from the perspective of psychological well-being. It contrasts the Confucian concepts of “Filial Piety”, “Fraternal Duty”, “Loyalty”, and “Worry” from the “Classic of Filial Piety” of the Yuan Dynasty with their Mongolian translations: taqimdaγu (representing “Filial Piety”), ǰoqi- (representing “Fraternal Duty”), činɡ ünen sedkil (representing “Loyalty”), and qoor ada (representing “Worry”). The Mongols live in a nomadic way and their sense of security and belonging mainly comes from their families. Therefore, Mongolian understanding of “filial piety” is limited to family members who are related by blood. The Han people live in a settled farming way and their sense of security and belonging comes not only from their own family members but also from external groups. Thus, the “filial piety” in Han culture has a richer connotation. The Mongols follow a system of electing a Khan based on merit and implement the youngest son inheritance system, which is no mandatory requirement for the relationship between brothers. The Han Chinese practice primogeniture to highlight the unquestioned authority of the eldest son. Concerning “Fraternal Duty”, the Mongols emphasize mutual care and love between brothers, while the Han people value their younger brothers for one-way obedience and reverence and the unequal status affects the intimate realtionships and psychological well-being of family members. As for “Loyalty”, the Mongolian democratic consultation demands that tribal leaders adhere to the contractual rules between them and the coalition leader, but the centralized monarchical system in Han society requires the absolute obedience to the monarch and even death for the monarch, which makes people feel anxious and panicked and greatly affects psychological well-being of ethnic groups. The Mongols believe in “Tenɡri” (the heavens) and think the “Worry” is the direct publishment of divinity on humans, while the Han Chinese believe that people can not commuticate directly with divinity and the “Worry” is the indirect publishment of divinity on humans. The belief in spiritual beings has a postive impact on the psychological well-being of ethnic groups. Results: The main reasons for the differences in Mongolian translation terms arise from life customs, religious beliefs, and social systems formed under the influence of psychological factors related to mental health, like psychological safety and the sense of psychological belonging. Conclusions: Future translation research should pay attention to the impact of cultural psychological factors on translation terminology in texts, further focusing on the psychological cognitive patterns and the mental health states of different ethnicities. This will add a new psychological research perspective to the field of translation studies. MHBM035: THE INFLUENCE OF INDUSTRIAL DIVERSIFICATION AND CHINA REGIONAL ECONOMIC RESILIENCE ON THE PSYCHOLOGICAL SECURITY OF URBAN RESIDENTS Xinya Tang a , Linlin Zhu a , Xinran Ye a , Beining Ying b,c , Qiantao Fan a a School of Economics and Management, Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, Hangzhou 310023, China, b School of Science, Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, Hangzhou 310023, China, c Institute of Science and Technology, CY Cergy Paris University, Cergy 95000, France Objective: This paper discusses the influence of industrial diversification and regional economic resilience on residents’ psychological security. Results: (1) There is an N-shaped curve relationship between industrial diversification and urban economic resilience, and entrepreneurial activity has a negative regulatory effect on the relationship between them. This conclusion still holds after a series of robustness tests; (2) Heterogeneity analysis shows that the entrepreneurial activity makes the N-shaped relationship between industrial diversification and urban economic resilience smooth before the impact, but it is not significant after the impact. In non-resource-based cities, entrepreneurial activity negatively regulates the N-shaped relationship between industrial diversification and urban economic resilience, but it is not significant in resource-based cities. (3) There is an N-curve relationship between industrial diversity and urban residents’ psychological security, and the results of regression analysis show that there is a positive relationship between the level of industrial diversity and urban residents’ psychological security. Conclusions: Industrial diversification can enhance the resilience of regional economy and make it more adaptable and risk-resistant. Industrial diversification can reduce the dependence of regional economy, improve the flexibility of economy and the ability to resist external shocks. In addition, industrial diversification can also enhance residents’ psychological security, make them more optimistic and confident about the future, and reduce the psychological pressure caused by economic fluctuations. MHBM038: THE APPLICATION EFFECT OF THE “YIN-YANG GUIDING” FOOT BATH METHOD IN MILD TO MODERATE INSOMNIA POPULATIONS Jingya Li a , Huanya Li b a Ministry of Civil Affairs Training Center, Beijing 102600, China, b Academy of Medical Sciences, Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan, Shanxi 030001, China. Background: Insomnia is the most common sleep disorder in clinical practice, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has various methods to treat insomnia. Based on traditional Chinese medicine theory, this study selects a cost-effective herbal foot bath as a primary treatment for primary insomnia. We observed its regulatory effect on mild to moderate insomnia to provide evidence for community sleep health management. Subjects and Methods: This study used a single-group target value method. Patients with mild to moderate insomnia were treated with an herbal foot bath, with a 7-day treatment considered one course. Participants were asked to soak their feet 1 hour before bedtime, avoiding doing so on an empty stomach and within 1 hour after meals. This was done 5 days a week. The herbal pack was brewed with boiling water. The water temperature should ideally be lowered to 45°C before use. The soaking time ranged between 20-30 minutes, with the water level 10cm above the ankles. Patients were followed up before and after the treatment to evaluate its application effect. Results: A total of 38 patients, 11 males (28.95%) and 27 females (71.05%) with mild to moderate insomnia were included. No adverse events were reported. The scores of components 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7, as well as the total score on the Pittsburgh scale, showed significant differences with P&lt;0.05. Conclusions: In traditional Chinese medicine, the normal sleep-wake mechanism is termed “Wu-Mi”, The core pathogenesis of insomnia is “Yin-Yang imbalance, Yang not merging with Yin.” Stimulating the related acupoints of the Yin Qiao meridian, selecting “Yang leading into Yin type” drugs and leading Yang into Yin can improve sleep. Through the herbal foot bath method, following the Qiao meridian operation rules and using “Yin-Yang guiding” herbs, the treatment was found to be effective for community patients with mild to moderate insomnia. However, due to a limited sample size, narrow observation scope, and singular efficacy indicators, the long-term therapeutic effects and impacts in other areas remain unclear. In the future, expanding the sample size, including more observation indicators, and if conditions permit, conducting a randomized double-blind controlled trial would further validate the results. Different combinations of the numbers of red balls and white balls were employed as the uncertainty manipulation. Participants in all conditions rated their enjoyment on a 15-point scale from -7 to 7. The experiments were carried out in a computer room. Results: Findings showed that the information presentation formatis a critical factor. There was a two-way interaction between the information presentation type and the level of uncertainty. Conclusions: A robust effect was observed on the presentation of enjoyment in psychological health and individual behavior. Information presentation type had a significant effect on the interaction of psychological enjoyment associated with the product type. The utilitarian prize will produce stronger enjoyment after a pictorial display than when it was described in writing. In addition, the results of this combined study have practical implications in relation to psychological health for alleviating individuals’ anxiety and depression. Moreover, according to the latest reports, there is a growing trend of anxiety disorders and depression spreading to the adolescent population. Faced with such widespread mental health issues, there are currently three effective coping paths: firstly, clinical medical diagnosis and treatment; the second is through the guidance and relief provided by psychologists and medical institutions; the third is through the approach of art therapy to alleviate inner anxiety and the tension between individuals, and the social environment. In the past, art therapy was often used as an auxiliary means of medical treatment, helping patients obtain psychological relief and spiritual healing. However, interdisciplinary thinking combines art therapy with education, social aesthetics, and other fields, forming a broader defense network. This allows ordinary individuals to obtain spiritual inspiration and psychological relief through participation in and exposure to artistic projects in their daily lives. This approach addresses the public mental health crisis stemming from social anxiety on a larger scale. Subjects and Methods: During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, students and teachers adopted a home-based online learning approach. These methods played a significant role in effective guidance and relief. After returning to school, these students brought their feelings and experiences from the course and participated in the “Mobile Hometown” project unit, part of the China Community Art Education Action Plan, conducted by Sichuan Fine Arts Institute. They presented their works in public spaces, impacting a wider audience through artistic expression. The works are displayed and presented in public spaces, where audiences can be inspired, moved, and resonated with by their emotive power. The mechanism of artistic therapy extends from individual practices’ cognitive reconstruction to the connection and co-creation in community art. Essentially, it is an expansion and extension of artistic therapeutic action. Through a project-based art practice model, the therapeutic function of art plays a greater role in public domains such as art galleries and communities, impacting a larger number of individuals. Conclusions: The online art classes during the pandemic served as an experimental sample for artistic therapy, uncovering the connection between art and action-oriented psychology. The integration of “cognitive behavioral therapy,” “behavioral motivation therapy,” and “exposure therapy” into various stages of artistic creation such as cognition, reflection, and visual transformation was explored. Art, as a distinctive medium of cognition and expression, is intricately linked with subtle shifts in the psyche. When attention is focused on the process rather than the final visual outcome, a plethora of psychological and emotional activities becomes visible. By regulating various psychological elements within the process, the purpose of art shifts from seeking visual aesthetic pleasure to becoming a mechanism for preventing and alleviating psychological issues like anxiety and depression. Particularly, when the presentation of art extends into larger public spaces, it can evoke emotional resonance in a broader audience. In a series of community art education initiatives, it becomes evident that the mechanisms of artistic therapy should be situated within the context of social spaces and local cultures. Within such a set of relationships, community art education practices transcend the practicalities of daily life during social interactions, reflecting the positive impact of psychological healing and the urgent need for mitigating social anxiety. MHBM060: ION CHANNELS IN CEREBRAL EDEMA: UNRAVELING MECHANISMS AND THERAPEUTIC PERSPECTIVES Yuan Yuan a,b,c , Zhiyong Tao d , Shunjie Zhong a,b,c , Guanghui Xu e , Xin Li f , Liang Liu a,b,c a Department of Neurosurgery, Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, No.25, Taiping Street, Luzhou City, Luzhou, 646000, China, b Neurosurgery Clinical Medical Research Center of Sichuan Province, Luzhou, 646000, China, c Neurosurgery Clinical Medical Research Center of Sichuan Province, Neurological Diseases and Brain Function Laboratory, Luzhou, 646000, China, d Meishan Tianfu New Area People’s Hospital, Shigao Street, Meishan City, 620000, China, e Department of Neurosurgery, Guang’an People’s Hospital, No.1, Section 4, Binhe Road, Guang’an District, Guang’an City,638000, China, f Department of Neurosurgery, Qu County People’s Hospital, No. 88 Heping Street, Qu County, Dazhou City, 635200, China. Background: Cerebral edema, or brain swelling, stands as a significant concern in the medical community due to its frequent occurrence following various central nervous system (CNS) insults. Particularly observed in conditions like traumatic brain injury (TBI) and excitotoxic injuries such as stroke, its ramifications are deeply concerning. The skull, unlike other parts of the body, lacks the flexibility to accommodate this swelling. As a result, the rigid structure of the skull exacerbates the detrimental impacts of edema, precipitating a rise in intracranial pressure. This surge in pressure compromises cerebral blood circulation, posing severe threats to neural health and function. Alarming statistics reveal that patients with severe stroke and TBI have mortality rates of up to 80% and 50%, respectively, within just a week following the incident. This highlights the dire need for effective therapeutic interventions. Regrettably, the therapeutic landscape remains limited. Present treatments tend to concentrate on alleviating the symptoms rather than targeting the root causes. Moreover, the general nature of these treatments often leads to unintended adverse side effects, arising from their lack of specificity in addressing the unique complexities of cerebral edema. Subjects and Methods: This comprehensive review focuses on the less-explored realm of ion channels and their potential roles in cerebral edema. We delve into the proposed functions of certain ion channels and transporters, namingly aquaporins, SUR1-TRPM4, chloride channels, glucose transporters, and proton-sensitive channels. These entities are studied in the context of their involvement in cerebral edema, particularly after acute ischemic stroke and TBI. Results: Ion channels and transporters appear to play pivotal roles in the mediation and exacerbation of cerebral edema following CNS injuries. By pinpointing their involvement, it becomes evident that they could serve as significant drug targets. Moreover, the review sheds light on various pharmacological inhibitors tailored for these specific targets, highlighting their potential in treating cerebral edema. Conclusions: The pathogenesis of cerebral edema following CNS injuries is intricately linked with the roles of specific ion channels and transporters. Recognizing this relationship offers promising avenues for therapeutic interventions. As we move towards a deeper understanding of edema formation mechanisms and the role of ion channels, the prospect of devising more targeted and efficacious therapeutic strategies to counter cerebral edema becomes increasingly plausible. MHBM064: MONGOLIAN MEDICINE JIRUHE-6 MODULATES THE Β3AR-NO-CGMP-PKG PATHWAY TO ATTENUATE HEART FAILURE IN RATS WITH COLD PATTERN SYNDROME Hua Li a , HuRiLeBaGen a , ARuNa a , GuiZhi a , JiangBa a , RuRong Li b , Wurichaifu a , Yongmei Meng c a School of Mongolian Medicine, Inner Mongolia Medical University, Hohhot, Inner Mongolia 010110, China, b Tongliao Centers for Disease Prevention and Control, Tongliao, Inner Mongolia 028005, China, c Graduate School of Inner Mongolia Medical University, Hohhot, Inner Mongolia 010110, China Background: This study investigates the therapeutic effects of the Mongolian medicine Anshen Buxin Liuwei Pill (Jiruhe-6, J6) on improving cardiac function in rats with cold pattern heart failure (HF) and its influence on the β3AR-NO-cGMP-PKG pathway. Subjects and Methods: Adult SPF-grade Wistar rats were randomly divided into a normal control group (Con) and a cold pattern heart failure group to establish the heart failure model (induced by intraperitoneal injection of doxorubicin hydrochloride followed by gavage with ice water). The successfully modeled rats were further randomly divided into the model group (Mod), J6 group, and digoxin group (Dig), each consisting of 8 rats. After intervention for 4 weeks, cardiac color Doppler ultrasound and HE staining of myocardial tissues were performed for pathological morphological examination. ELISA was used to measure serum levels of N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP), and myocardial tissue nitric oxide (NO) concentration. The activities of nitric oxide synthase (NOS), sodium-potassium-ATPase(Na+-K+-ATP),calcium-ATPase(Ca2+-ATP),and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) in myocardial tissues were also assessed. Western blot was used to detect protein kinase G (PKG) expression, and qPCR was employed to measure the expression of β3 adrenergic receptor (β3AR) mRNA. Results: showed that, compared to the Con group, the Mod group exhibited elevated serum levels of NT-proBNP and cGMP (P&lt;0.01). At the same time,cardiac color Doppler ultrasound parameters (EFand FS), myocardial Na+-K+-ATP, Ca2+-ATP, SDH, NOS activities, NO, and β3AR mRNA expression were decreased (P&lt;0.01), and PKG expression was downregulated. In comparison to the Mod group, rats in the J6 and Dig groups showed increased EF,FS,myocardial Na+-K+-ATP, Ca2+-ATP, SDH, NOS activities, NO, and β3AR mRNA expression, as well as elevated serum cAMP levels (P&lt;0.01), and reduced serum NT-proBNP and cGMP levels (P&lt;0.05). Additionally, the expression of PKG in myocardial tissues was upregulated. Compared to the Con group, the Mod group rats exhibited disordered myocardial cell arrangement, inflammatory cell infiltration, and myocardial fibrosis. However, these pathological changes were significantly alleviated in the J6 and Dig groups. Conclusions: Thus, the Mongolian medicine J6 exerts its anti-heart failure effects by modulating the β3AR-NO-cGMP-PKG pathway. Subjects and Methods: This paper relies on the restorative theory of environmental psychology, uses a variety of approaches including literature review, questionnaire survey and mathematical analysis. The impacts of virtual tourism experience on tourists’ psychological stress and emotions were also investigated. Results: the following results were obtained from this research: (1) During the tests, a 15 minutes virtual tour experience was found to be able to bring better emotional recovery for the participants and help relieve stress and negative emotions, and induce positive emotions. (2) At the end of the virtual tourism experience, differences in place of residence affected emotional recovery from the virtual tourism experience, and living in a rural area was more helpful in alleviating negative emotions. It was found that participation in virtual tourism activities resulted in significantly lower negative emotions in rural than in urban populations, while there were no significant differences in stress and positive emotions. Conclusions: According to restorative theory and supported by virtual reality technology, this research examined the effects of virtual tourism experience on people’s psychological stress and emotions through repeated measures ANOVA. Belanga No.1 Simp. JL Ayahanda 80234, Medan, Indonesia, b Department of General Surgery, Yan’an University Affiliated Hospital (Xi’an Daxing Hospital.), 353 Labor North Road, Lianhu District, 710000, Shaanxi, China, c Department of Cardiovascular Medicine, Xuanhan County Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Dazhou 636150, Sichuan, China. Objective: Colon cancer refers to the malignant tumor of the epithelial cells of the colon, including malignant tumors of the right colon, left colon, transverse colon, and rectum. Colorectal cancer (CRC) or malignant tumor of the large intestine is one of the most common malignant tumors of the digestive system worldwide, posing a serious threat to human health and life. Due to insufficient understanding of colorectal cancer, a lack of emphasis on health education, failure to promote preventive measures, and a reduction in risk factors associated with colorectal cancer, early screening for colorectal cancer is not commonly practiced. These factors contribute to patients being diagnosed with colorectal cancer in its advanced stages, often involving invasion or metastasis to surrounding tissues and organs. The study of all advanced colorectal cancer cases invading the urogenital system has research significance. Subjects and Methods: Familiarize oneself with the anatomical relationships between the urogenital system and the surrounding structures of the colon and rectum. Encourage everyone to review and summarize the comprehensive clinical manifestations associated with advanced colorectal cancer invading the urogenital system, explore new treatment approaches for such patients, standardize the treatment process for this patient population, and bring new therapeutic hope to the patients. Results: Through our research, we have gained an understanding of the close relationship between the colon and surrounding tissues and organs. When advanced colorectal cancer invades surrounding tissues and organs, a complex set of symptoms may manifest. Patients with such conditions require multiple systemic examinations during their assessments. The treatment principle for these patients involves surgical resection of the colon cancer along with the involved surrounding tissues and organs. A current novel treatment strategy involves administering hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) to patients preoperatively to achieve downstaging of the advanced tumor. Subsequent to tumor downstaging, patients can undergo curative surgery, followed by postoperative HIPEC to reduce the spread of tumor cells. It is important to note that these treatment measures currently lack sufficient support from relevant literature and are primarily reported in isolated cases, demonstrating effectiveness. Therefore, substantial prospective research is still needed to validate these approaches. Conclusions: There is no standardized treatment protocol for advanced colorectal cancer invading or metastasizing to the urogenital system. Individual treatment plans and strategies vary significantly. Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) has been shown to be effective in downstaging tumors and controlling intraoperative tumor cell spread in patients with advanced colorectal cancer, with most evidence coming from individual studies. Currently, there is a lack of large-scale prospective experimental research. Conducting research in this area is highly necessary, and further exploration is affirmative. Future experimental data will likely demonstrate the superiority of this new treatment strategy. Results: Firstly, these corruption cases have distinct characteristics. Bribery is the highest proportion of corruption patterns here. Secondly, there are several main psychological health reasons for corruption. They include the negative personality, life pressure, work anxiety, career setbacks, vanity, inferiority complex, arrogant mentality, emotional instability, social setbacks, and other external factors of these corrupt officials. This inner insecurity may lead to problems in their mental health and even affect their daily life and work. Conclusions: The findings suggest that illegal activities in the Courier business and the tobacco-related intelligence study had a negative impact on the mental health of participants. People engaged in the express delivery industry face psychological pressure and anxiety. In order to strengthen public mental health awareness and literacy, ensure the safety and trust of customers, effectively respond to illegal activities, and maintain social security and stability, it is necessary to improve the mental health awareness of practitioners, carry out mental health education and training, help practitioners understand and cope with psychological pressure at work, provide psychological counseling and support services, and solve mental health problems in a timely manner. Background: Sleeping health involves various systems throughout the body and is closely related to cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, reproductive health. Then, this paper conducted experiments to study the influence of mattress materials on the sleep comfort of people with different body sizes. Eight usual mattresses were selected, and four types of subjects were based on BMI for body pressure distribution testing, subjective evaluation of comfort, subjective and objective correlation analysis. The pressure distribution was measured using a Tekscan body pressure measurement system (BPMS). Peak pressure and average pressure were calculated based on recorded pressure distribution data. Peak pressure is the maximum pressure on the mattress. The average pressure is the mean value of all pressures on the mattress. In the physical properties of mattress materials, peak pressure and average pressure can reflect the sleeping comfort of subjects. The pressure sensing mat was placed on the subjects’ whole body and experimental mattress. When the pressure value was stable, the test was recorded for 30 minutes, and each experiment was repeated 3 times. After pressure distribution, the subjects did the subjective evaluation through subjective status and evaluation of each part. Results: The trend of pressure value and contact area changes was consistent among different body types of subjects, with higher pressure value and smaller contact area on cotton and palm mattresses. The pressure value was the lowest, and the contact area was the largest on water and air mattresses. The slim and obese subjects were more sensitive to mattress performance than expected and overweight subjects. The slim subjects had higher gradient values on water and air mattresses, while obese subjects had higher gradient values on cotton and palm mattresses. Conclusions: It was found that different mattress materials have different comfort evaluations for different body types of subjects in the supine position. The results proved that the slim and obese subjects were more sensitive to mattress materials. The slim subjects preferred memory foam mattress and latex mattress. The normal body shape subjects preferred memory foam mattress and sponge mattress. The overweight subjects preferred memory foam, sponge, and air mattresses. The obese subjects preferred memory foam mattress and air mattress. MHBM125: A STUDY ON THE EFFECTS OF PILLOW SIZE, MATERAL AND SHAPE ON SLEEP HEALTH Jianjun Hou a , Yichao Mao a , Yu Tang a a School of Art and Design, Nanjing Institute of Technology, Nanjing, Jiang Su, China. Background: Sleep problems are one of the most common health issues affecting the general public, with close associations to psychological disorders, cognitive impairments, physical dysfunctions, and a wide range of other medical conditions. Sleep health is influenced by various factors, including psychological elements, environmental conditions, bedding materials, external disruptions, and work pressure. Among these factors, pillows play a crucial role in providing support to the neck, alleviating neck tension, and promoting restorative sleep. Pillow performance attributes include pillow height, material, and shape. Subjects and Methods: This study began with a comprehensive theoretical examination of sleep-related issues and the multifaceted factors influencing sleep health. It systematically explored the relationship between pillows and sleep health, encompassing research findings related to pillow height, material, and shape. For the pillow height experiment, 9 different pillow heights ranging from 5 to 13 cm were selected. In the pillow material experiment, 5 different materials were chosen for the pillows: chemical fiber, buckwheat skin, latex, memory sponge, and inflatable pillow. In the pillow shape experiment, 5 different pillow shapes were selected: flat, cubic, S-shape, concave, and convex. The Tekscan body pressure measurement system (BPMS) served as the experimental instrument. Peak pressure and average pressure were calculated based on recorded pressure distribution data. After the pressure distribution assessments, subjects provided subjective evaluations. Results: Pillow Height Experiment Results: Pillows with a height ranging from 6 to 7 cm exhibited lower average and peak pressures, along with higher comfort ratings across various body parts. Conversely, pillow height of 13 cm had the highest-pressure index and received the lowest subjective evaluation. Pillow Material Experiment Results: Pillows constructed from memory foam and latex showed evenly distributed pressure on the head and neck, lower overall body pressure values. In contrast, inflatable pillows displayed more concentrated pressure, greater firmness, reduced elasticity, and received lower overall ratings. Pillow Shape Experiment Results: The S-shape pillow consistently received the highest comfort ratings for all body parts which can improve sleep health, followed by the convex and flat-shape pillows. The cube-shape pillow concentrated pressure on the posterior of the head, resulting in smaller contact areas on the head and neck. Conclusions: In summary, pillow height, material, and shape have a significant impact on overall sleep health. Choosing a suitable pillow can increase the relief of sleep disorders and improve sleep health. Pillows with heights between 6 and 7 cm had higher comfort evaluations. Pillows made from memory foam and latex exhibited superior comfort attributes, including lower body pressure values, moderate firmness, and good elasticity. Pillows filled with buckwheat skin provided adequate neck support, larger contact areas. The S-shape pillow consistently received the highest comfort ratings across all body regions, followed by the convex and flat-shape pillows. MHBM129: EMPIRICAL STUDY ON THE IMPACT OF FITNESS QIGONG COMBINED WITH STRENGTH TRAINING ON THE BALANCE ABILITY OF THE ELDERLY Shengfeng Xue a , Xi Yang b , Yicheng Nie c , Chunjian Chen d , Xue Zheng a , Xiaoyi Xu a a Nanjing Research Institute of Sports Science, Nanjing, China, b Department of Rehabilitation, Zhongda Hospital, School of Medicine, Southeast University, Nanjing, China, c Nanjing Sport Institute, Nanjing, China, d Nanjing Health Qigong Management Center, Nanjing, China. SX and XY contributed equally to this study. Objective : To investigate the positive effects of traditional fitness qigong combined with muscle strength training on enhancing the balance ability of the elderly. Methods: 80 healthy elderly individuals aged 60-69 were randomly divided into traditional fitness qigong group, strength training group, and integrated intervention group. The traditional fitness qigong group underwent 12 weeks of fitness qigong “Ba Duan Jin” practice, three times a week, 40 minutes each session. The strength training group followed a designated training plan for 12 weeks, three times a week, 40 minutes each session. The integrated intervention group first practiced “Ba Duan Jin” for 20 minutes, rested for 10 minutes, and then selected from the strength training group’s plan, omitting the warm-up phase of strength training, with everything else remaining consistent. They practiced three times a week for a continuous 12 weeks. The balance function, muscle strength, walking ability, and physical fitness indicators were observed and analyzed before and after the intervention in the three groups. Results: Regarding static balance, the integrated intervention group scored the highest in closed-eye single-leg standing and enhanced Romberg test results, with a significant difference compared to the other two groups (p&lt;0.05). For dynamic balance, the “stand-up-walk” test time was shortest in the integrated intervention group, and there was a significant difference compared to both the strength training group and traditional fitness qigong group (P&lt;0.05). The on-the-spot closed-eye stepping score was best in the traditional fitness qigong group, and there was a significant difference compared to the integrated intervention group and strength training group (P&lt;0.05). In terms of muscle strength, the 30s sit-to-stand count was highest in the strength training group, with a statistically significant difference compared to the other two groups (P&lt;0.05). The difference between the integrated intervention group and the traditional fitness qigong group was also statistically significant (P&lt;0.05). For physical fitness, the reaction time was shortest in the strength training group, and there was a significant difference compared to the other two groups (P&lt;0.05). The seated forward bend length was highest in the traditional fitness qigong group, and there was a significant difference compared to the integrated intervention group and strength training group (P&lt;0.05). Regarding walking ability, the 6-meter walking speed test score was highest in the integrated intervention group, with a significant difference compared to the other two groups (P&lt;0.05). The difference between the strength training group and traditional fitness qigong group was also significant (P&lt;0.05). Conclusion: Traditional fitness qigong combined with strength training integrates the advantages of strength training and fitness qigong “Ba Duan Jin” practice. It can stimulate the neuromuscular system more comprehensively and is an efficient method to enhance the balance ability of the elderly and prevent falls. We employ three distinct sampling techniques: random sampling, oversampling, and undersampling. Regression and random forest (RF) were employed as the classifiers. The combination of variable selection, sampling method, and model method resulted in 18 cases. Results: The best AUC index achieved a value of 0.671, and it aligns with the selection of variable selection scenarios S2, which was sampled in a undersampling manner and modeled using xgbTree. It was determined that the most favorable specificity performance is 0.867. This index value corresponds to the variable selection scenario S1, which is sampled in an oversampling manner and subsequently modeled in xgbTree. Conclusions: This paper identified AJCC v7 disease staging, T stage, metastatic number of lymph nodes, positive rate of lymph nodes, and tumor nodules as the key factors impacting the recurrence rate of D2R0 in gastric cancer. Considering the AUC and sensitivity performance, xgbTree utilizing the undersampling technique has been identified as the most advantageous modeling result. In terms of oversampling, xgbTree outperformed all other options when considering specific performance indicators. As a result, the xgbTree method outperforms in this study. Our research provides a practical way to identify and analyze risk factors of postoperative recurrence rate of gastric cancer D2R0 operation for the whole system. There is a significant low degree negative correlation between standing long jump and one minute sit up scores and MPAI index (r=-0.35, -0.31, P&lt;0.01). Tai Chi can effectively help mobile phone addicted college students improve their physical health, especially flexibility and aerobic endurance; The degree of physical decline in boys is greater than that in girls; The main reasons why mobile phone addiction affects physical health are poor usage posture and bad habits. It is recommended to enhance the prevention awareness of mobile phone addiction among college students, carry out health education on mobile phone addiction, and develop reasonable treatment measures to help college students break free from their dependence on mobile phones. MHBM147: A STUDY OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CALLIGRAPHY EDUCATION IN PROMOTING THE MENTAL HEALTH OF INTERNATIONAL CHINESE LEARNERS Guirong He a , Xu Liu a a China International Language and Culture College, Krirk University, Bangkok 10220, Thailand Background: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of calligraphy education on the emotional state and self-esteem of international Chinese language learners. Methods: This study utilized a pre- and post-test experimental design and recruited a sample of 300 international Chinese language learners aged 18 to 30 years old from different countries and regions through both online and offline channels. The experimental group participated in a calligraphy education program, with two offline classes per week, totaling 2 hours of learning time each time for 8 weeks. The main content of the calligraphy education program was calligraphy technique, chapter style, and artwork form, which included Chinese characters, poems, calligraphy appreciation, and creative learning. The teaching process emphasized the use of the fun of calligraphy stories. The control group received no relevant calligraphy education. The learners’ emotional state and self-esteem level were assessed by using publicly available and validated scales, such as the Zung Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) and the Ten-Item Personality Inventory (TIPI). Results: After data collection and analysis, it was found that learners in the experimental group showed significant improvement in their emotional state after the course. Specifically, the emotional state scores of the learners in the experimental group improved from 3.2 (standard deviation 0.5) before the lesson to 4.8 (standard deviation 0.6) after the lesson, which presented a statistically significant difference compared to before the lesson (t = 12.34, p &lt; 0.001). In contrast, there was no statistically significant change in the emotional state scores of the learners in the control group (mean score of 3.4 with a standard deviation of 0.4 before the lesson; mean score of 3.6 with a standard deviation of 0.5 after the lesson, t = 1.05, p = 0.250). These data results support the significant improvement in the emotional state of the learners in the experimental group. It was also observed that the experimental group learners’ self-esteem improved significantly. Self-esteem scores improved from 2.9 (standard deviation 0.4) before the class to 3.8 (standard deviation 0.5) after the class, which was a significant difference compared to the preclass (t = 8.76, p &lt; 0.001). In contrast, there was no statistically significant change in the self-esteem scores of the learners in the control group (mean score of 3.0, standard deviation 0.3 before the lesson; mean score of 3.1, standard deviation 0.4 after the lesson, t = 0.78, p = 0.432). The results suggest that calligraphy education has a positive impact on the mental health of international Chinese learners. Conclusions: Through participation in the calligraphy education program, learners’ emotions were soothed and positively adjusted, while self-esteem was enhanced. This emphasizes the importance of calligraphy education in the language learning process and highlights its potential for mental health promotion. This study provides new perspectives on educational practices and future research in related fields. MHBM152: CLINICAL OBSERVATION OF HYDRAULIC DILATION COMBINED WITH MEDICAL CHITOSAN INJECTION FOR FROZEN SHOULDER DURING PAINFUL PHASE Meixian Peng a , Yidong Yu a , Qiuye Ma a , Yi Luo b , Qiang Zeng c a Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital of Jiulongpo District, Jiulongpo 400051, Chongqing, China, b The first branch of the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China, c Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital of Wanzhou District, Chongqing, China Objective: To observe the clinical effects of hydraulic dilation combined with medical chitosan injection for the treatment of frozen shoulder during the painful phase. Methods: 135 patients diagnosed with frozen shoulder during the painful phase were randomly divided into: (i) Group 1: Hydraulic dilation + Medical chitosan injection (45 cases); (ii) Group 2: Simple hydraulic dilation (45 cases); (iii) Group 3: Simple medical chitosan injection (45 cases). All groups received one treatment. The Frozen Shoulder Assessment Scale was used to evaluate the patients before (0d), 1 day after treatment, and at 1, 2, 3, and 4 weeks post-treatment, and any complications during the treatment period were observed among the three groups. Results: The difference in efficacy scores between different time points before and after treatment was statistically significant, indicating a time effect (F=4,746.790, P=0.000). There was an interaction effect between the time factor and the group factor (F=166.330, P=0.000). The overall inter-group differences in efficacy scores were statistically significant, indicating a group effect (F=1,840.730, P=0.000). Apart from before treatment, the efficacy scores of the three groups at other time points showed statistically significant differences. One day and 1, 2, 3, and 4 weeks after treatment, the scores of Group 1 were higher than those of Groups 2 and 3. The scores of Groups 2 and 3 reached the recovery standard 3 weeks after treatment, while the score of Group 1 reached the recovery standard 1 week after treatment. Conclusion: The combination of hydraulic dilation and medical chitosan injection can quickly relieve shoulder pain symptoms and improve joint function in patients with frozen shoulder during the painful phase. Compared with hydraulic dilation and medical chitosan injection alone, it has a faster onset, better efficacy, and higher safety, making it worthy of clinical promotion and application.
