MHBM155: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN COLLEGE STUDENTS’ PHYSICAL ACTIVITY BEHAVIOUR AND INTERPERSONAL SKILLS - THE CHAIN MEDIATING ROLE OF MENTAL TOUGHNESS AND COPING STYLES Fulei Wang a , Zhao Chen b , Jun Zhao c , Xin Chen c a Henan Smart Sports Development Co., Ltd, Zhengzhou, Henan 450000, China, b College of Physical Education, Zhengzhou University of Light Industry, Zhengzhou, Henan 450001, China, c Shandong Sport University, Jinan, Shandong 250102, China Background: The relationship between physical activity behaviour and interpersonal skills among university students has been of interest because of its significance for both mental health and social life. Research has explored the mediating role of mental toughness and coping styles in this relationship. Mental toughness can help college students better cope with stress and frustration in life, while positive coping styles can help improve interpersonal skills. Objective To explore the relationship between mental toughness, coping styles in college students’ physical activity behaviour and interpersonal skills. Objective: The aim of this study was to delve into the relationship between mental toughness and coping styles in the field of mental health on college students’ physical activity behaviours and interpersonal skills. Subjects and Methods: Using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the Interpersonal Skills Questionnaire, the Mental Toughness Scale, and the Simple Coping Styles Questionnaire, a survey study was conducted on 796 university students, of whom 408 were male and 388 were female. Results: (1) There was a significant positive correlation between the two variables of physical activity behaviour, mental toughness, positive coping styles and interpersonal skills of university students (r of 0.104-0.670, P &lt; 0.01). (2) Mental toughness and positive coping styles had a significant mediating effect between physical activity behaviour and interpersonal competence, with a standardised total indirect effect value of 0.0024, accounting for 100 percent of the total effect value. Specifically, the mediating effect between physical activity behaviour and interpersonal competence consisted of two paths: physical activity behaviour → mental toughness → interpersonal competence as indirect effect path 1 (effect value of 0.0022); physical activity behaviour → mental toughness → positive coping style → interpersonal competence as indirect effect path 2 (effect value of 0.0002). The percentages of the two indirect effect paths in the total effect value were 91.7 percent and 8.3 percent, respectively. Conclusions: College students’ physical activity behaviours do not directly predict interpersonal competence, but mental toughness and positive coping styles act as chain mediators in the relationship between physical activity behaviours and interpersonal competence. MHBM159: AN OVERVIEW OF THE RESEARCH ON THE ETHICAL ISSUES OF INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND MENTAL HEALTH IN THE ALGORITHMIC ERA Boyu Zheng a a School of Public Management, Hohai University, Nanjing, Jiangsu 210000, China. Background: With the development of the Internet, personalized recommendation algorithm gradually rises, which makes people more likely to fall into the information cocoon, only accessible to the information related to their own interests, and thus they would be lack of cognition of different views and diversity. In addition, the problems of excessive and unbalanced information acquisition, false information and the spread of rumors have become increasingly prominent. Therefore, this study aims to explore the impacts of these ethical issues on mental health. Subjects and Methods: This study, combined with existing research results and expert opinions, adopts comprehensive research methods, including literature review and analysis, to conduct a comprehensive analysis of ethical issues of information communication and their impacts on mental health. Results: First of all, the guiding role of information cocoon is an ethical issue worthy of attention. Due to the existence of personalized recommendation algorithms, people are only exposed to information that matches their interests in most cases, and that’s how the information cocoons are formed. This kind of information filtering will lead to individuals’ lack of cognition of different views and diversity, which is easy for the occurrence of rigid thinking and cognitive bias, and then affect their mental health. Secondly, excessive and unbalanced accesses to information is also an important ethical issue. In the age of algorithms, people can gain lots of information anytime and anywhere, but the quality and authenticity of the information are difficult to guarantee. Prolonged exposure to false information, low-quality content and malicious rumors can cause psychological problems such as anxiety, confusion and fatigue. In addition, excessive focus on negative information and illusory perfect lives on social media may also trigger mental health issues such as low self-esteem and depression. Finally, false information and the spread of rumors are serious ethical issues. Although the Internet provides more information channels, it is also prone to misinformation and rumors. The spread of such false information and rumors will bring psychological burdens such as anxiety, fear and confusion to individuals, and may even lead to social isolation and trust crisis. Conclusions: Comprehensive studies have shown that ethical issues of information dissemination in the age of algorithms pose challenges to mental health. In order to protect the mental health of individuals, it is necessary to strengthen the awareness and regulation of the ethical issues of information communication. At the same time, it is also crucial to promote transparent and responsible dissemination of information, which can be achieved by establishing sound regulatory mechanisms and strengthening education and training. In addition, it is also necessary to improve users’ information literacy and critical thinking skills, which can help individuals better identify and understand information, thus reducing the incidence of mental health problems. Only in this way can we realize the sound development of information dissemination and ensure that individuals have good mental health in the information age. MHBM180: PROTEOMIC STUDY OF ELECTROACUPUNCTURE IN REGULATING FERROPTOSIS, BLADDER NECK FIBROSIS, AND URINATION FUNCTION AFTER SUPRASACRAL SPINAL CORD INJURY Jincan Liu a , Liya Tang a , Xiaoying Sun a , Qirui Qu a , Qiong Liu a , Lu Zhou b , Hong Zhang a , Bruce Song c , Ming Xu a , Kun Ai a a College of Acupuncture, Massage and Rehabilitation, Hunan University of Chinese Medicine, Changsha, Hunan 410208, China, b Department of rehabilitation medicine, Chenzhou first people’s Hospital, Chenzhou, Hunan 423000, China, c Key Laboratory of Sports and Physical Health Ministry of Education, Beijing Sport University, Beijing 100084, China. JCL and LYT contributed equally to this study. Background: Uprasacral spinal cord injury (SSCI) often leads to bladder dysfunction, which can significantly impact the quality of life of affected individuals. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been proposed as a potential therapeutic approach for SSCI-related bladder dysfunction, but the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. The aim of this study was to explore whether electroacupuncture regulates phenotypic transformation of smooth muscle cells by inhibiting ferroptosis and inhibiting fibrosis, thereby improving bladder urination function after suprasacral spinal cord injury. Subjects and Methods: In this study, we employed a rat model of suprasacral spinal cord injury (SSCI) and categorized the rats into four distinct groups: sham, SSCI, SSCI+EA (Electroacupuncture), and SSCI+EA+Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1). Following a 10-day period of electroacupuncture intervention, we conducted urodynamic assessments to evaluate bladder functionality and applied Masson’s trichrome staining to assess the degree of bladder neck fibrosis. Additionally, we conducted tandem mass tag (TMT)-based quantitative proteomics analysis, Western blot (WB) detection, and ferrous ion concentration analysis to elucidate the potential mechanisms underlying the effects of electroacupuncture on bladder function. Results: Urodynamic results showed that electroacupuncture could improve the micturition function of NB rat bladders, and HE staining showed that pathological changes, such as inflammation of bladder neck tissue, were improved after electroacupuncture intervention. Proteomics and biological information analysis show that ferroptosis and the contractile smooth muscle cell marker SMTN were significantly enriched (P&lt;0.05). WB analysis showed that after electroacupuncture treatment, the expressions of STEAP3, TF, TFRC, DMT1 and P53 decreased significantly (P&lt;0.05), while the expression of SMTN increased significantly (P&lt;0.05).The ferrous ion concentration detection results showed that the ferrous ion concentration in the bladder neck tissue decreased significantly after electroacupuncture treatment (P&lt;0.01). Masson’s trichrome staining showed that the deposition of collagen fibers in the bladder neck muscle layer decreased significantly after electroacupuncture treatment (P&lt;0.01). Conclusions: Our study offers compelling evidence that electroacupuncture (EA) treatment not only ameliorates bladder dysfunction but also mitigates bladder neck fibrosis in suprasacral spinal cord injury (SSCI) rats. This beneficial effect can be attributed to EA’s ability to prevent the transition of bladder neck smooth muscle cells from a contractile to a synthetic phenotype by inhibiting iron metabolism. Consequently, this inhibition of iron metabolism curtails bladder neck fibrosis, enhances bladder neck compliance, and ultimately leads to improved bladder voiding function following SSCI. These findings underscore the potential of EA as a promising therapeutic modality for addressing SSCI-related bladder dysfunction. The good implementation of the Measures for Assessing the Security of Data Exit is sufficient to satisfy the public’s psychological need for data exit security. The key to the source of public anxiety is the ability of data processors to strictly comply with the requirements of the Measures when conducting self-assessments. Conclusions: It is recommended that a professional and credible third-party assessment mechanism be established with reference to the practice of comparative law, so as to make up for the inadequacy of the current system which does not set up monitoring or alternative measures for the self-assessment system, as well as to adequately safeguard the public’s psychological need for the security of the data out of the country. MHBM196: EXPRESSION PROFILE OF PXR AND CAR IN MOUSE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM Pan Xiong a , Changhao Lin b , Yang Liu a a Department of Neurosurgery, Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, Luzhou 646000, People’s Republic of China, b Department of Neurosurgery, Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College, Nanchong 637000, People’s Republic of China. PX and CHL contributed equally to this study. Background: PXR (Pregnane X Receptor) is a member of the nuclear receptor family and, together with CAR (Constitutive Androstane Receptor), is responsible for regulating the expression of proteins involved in substance metabolism and excretion. Previous research on PXR and CAR has primarily focused on areas such as drug metabolism, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. However, the expression and distribution of PXR and CAR in the central nervous system have remained unclear. The purpose of this study is to investigate the distribution of PXR and CAR in the brain, with the aim of providing experimental support for the prevention and treatment of central nervous system diseases or functional disorders. Subjects and Methods: This study included a total of 40 male rats (280-300g, 10 weeks old). The research examined the mRNA levels of PXR and CAR in rat brain tissues using QPCR (Quantitative real-time PCR). Additionally, immunohistochemistry assays were conducted to assess the protein expression levels of these receptors in rat brain tissues. Finally, in situ hybridization was employed for further validation. Results: The QPCR results indicate significant CAR mRNA expression in the cerebral cortex, hypothalamus, hippocampus, olfactory bulb, and spinal cord, while PXR expression in the rat brain is relatively low. Immunohistochemistry results on rat brain tissue slices show prominent CAR protein expression in regions such as the hippocampal CA3 area, Purkinje cell layer, interpositus cerebellar nucleus (Int), and lateral cerebellar nucleus (Lat). Furthermore, in the rat choroid plexus, both CAR and PXR exhibit strong positive expression. The results of the FISH (Fluorescence in situ hybridization) experiment align with the above findings, confirming CAR expression in the hippocampus and Purkinje cell layer of the cerebellum, while PXR mRNA was not detected in rat brain tissue. Conclusions: CAR and PXR are distributed in the hippocampus, cerebral cortex, and Purkinje cell layer of the cerebellum in the central nervous system of adult rats, with relatively low PXR expression. Based on a substantial body of preliminary research, we have formulated a hypothesis that CAR and PXR may be associated not only with behavioral activities but also with neurodegenerative diseases. These two nuclear receptors could potentially serve as therapeutic targets for neurological disorders. Background: In the past 3 years, a major public health crisis profoundly affected the physical and mental well-being of China’s residents. And it also crashed the stability of China’s economy, leading to severe short-term economic fluctuations, and along with economic recession and unemployment. The dual impact of this major public health crisis on the national healthcare system and the economy made people face enormous uncertainty, causing them not only to worry about health issues, but also about unemployment and income decline, which in turn has led to a significant decline in people’s subjective well-being.. Subjects and Methods: How long did it take for China’s economy to recover to its development status before the crisis? The main purpose of this paper is to try to answer this question through analyzing the national economic resilience in China, and then to derive some implications for improving the subjective well-being. To achieve this goal, this paper firstly reviews the progress of this major public health crisis and the corresponding economic policies in China, and then studies the national economic resilience of China in macroeconomic, industrial and financial dimensions, by analysing the economic recovery trajectory in these three dimensions after the huge shock. After that, we also make a discussion about the implications for subjective well-being promotion. Results: It took China about two years to recover the development status of macro-economy, industrial structure and financial system to that before the major public health crisis. Although the economy has quickly recovered after being impacted by the pandemic, the subjective well-being of residents has not rebounded as quickly. The subjective well-being of the people is closely related to the economic development. Conclusions: China’s economy recovered in a short time after the huge shock of major public health crisis, which shows strong national economic resilience. And it benefits from: first, the strong economic foundation has been built in past decades; second, the policies adopted by China, namely resolute epidemic governance, effective fiscal policy and flexible monetary policy. But this economic fluctuation still has a huge impact on the subjective well-being of the residents in China during the pandemic. So, we derived these following implications for subjective well-being: (1) Local governments should adopt different policies for residents of different groups and help them return to normal life as soon as possible, assist businesses in overcoming difficulties, and thereby enhance their subjective well-being. (2) The government should try its best to eliminate the troubles and anxieties caused by false information to residents. (3) The government should improve the quality of local public services to enhance residents’ subjective well-being. MHBM201: RESEARCH SUGGESTIONS OF ART THERAPY INTERVENTION ON MENTAL HEALTH OF COLLEGE STUDENTS IN SHANGHAI Yifan Cao a a Shanghai Publishing and Printing College, Shanghai, China. Background: In recent years, with the rapid development of society and the increasingly fierce competition, the mental health problems of college students in China have become increasingly prominent, and the mental health problems of college students have attracted much attention, which has become an urgent social problem to be solved. College students are facing pressure from learning, interpersonal communication and social competition, which has brought great challenges to their mental health. Especially after the new crown epidemic, college students’ psychological problems are particularly prominent. College students are more vulnerable than other groups due to their lack of life experience, limited psychological endurance, lack of stability and cognitive ability to be improved in the face of public health events, at present, Chinese society is in the stage of rapid transformation. The rapid development of the Internet and mobile devices makes it easier for college students to indulge in the virtual world. College students are facing the adaptation problems of academic pressure, employment pressure and social role transformation, while they are deeply affected by the Internet and indulge in the Internet. These problems all lead to the high incidence of psychological problems among college students in society. The urgency of this issue has gradually become apparent. Subjects and Methods: College Student Psychological Scale and Interviews. The research basis of this paper is the general psychological test of freshmen in Shanghai Publishing and Printing College. This test aims to understand the psychological status, personality characteristics, mental health level, etc. Provide artistic healing activities for future college students, the data analysis and tracking of artistic healing effects; Group counseling and heart rate variability (HRV) detector are used to track the data of students with psychological disorders through art therapy group counseling. After each art therapy, a 5-minute short-term HRV test is conducted on college students with psychological disorders using a heart rate variability (HRV) detector to collect data and analyze the patient’s sympathetic, parasympathetic, and autonomic nervous system balance, Obtain specific data on the effectiveness of artistic healing interventions. Results: Art therapy in the treatment of College Students’ psychological problems can help college students alleviate emotional problems, improve self-awareness and self-worth, promote social communication and emotional communication, and improve college students’ creativity and imagination through art therapy. Therefore, it is imperative to promote an art therapy intervention for psychological disorders among college students. Conclusions: Psychological health is not only related to individuals, but also to the entire society. Healthy psychological health can promote harmonious coexistence between individuals and others, reduce conflicts and violent behavior, and promote social stability and development. The intervention of art therapy in the psychological problems of college students is gradually being accepted by society. This article will analyze and construct a “trinity” linkage mechanism and decision-making suggestions from the perspective of the “responsibilities and rights” of hospitals, universities, and art institutions, in order to help art therapy enter universities and alleviate the psychological distress of college students. MHBM202: A STUDY ON THE LANDSCAPE DESIGN OF PRIMARY SCHOOL WALLS BASED ON CHILDREN’S PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH Zhiwei Tang a , Xiaoqiong Su a , Cheng Li b a Hunan Biological and Electromechanical polytechnic, Changsha, 410127, China, b Hunan Mass Media Vocational and Technical College, Changsha, 410000, China. Background: This paper aims to explore the importance of environmental education in talent cultivation. The methods of education can be divided into verbal teaching, role modeling, and environmental education, among which environmental education can provide a stable and comfortable environment for educators, enabling them to focus more on the practice of verbal teaching and role modeling. With the rapid development of China’s economy, the architectural landscape of campuses is also changing, especially the completion of new schools often brings visual and psychological changes and impacts to people, gradually forming the talent cultivation goal of “artistic life, art of living”. The landscape of primary school campuses, as an important place for children’s daily life, also has a significant impact on children’s mental health. At present, the design of primary school campus walls in China is relatively single, which can no longer meet the increasing psychological needs of children. Therefore, this study combines psychological needs and subjective well-being with the design of primary school campus wall landscapes, and summarizes a wall landscape design model that can meet the psychological needs of primary school campus landscape users based on theory and field research. By breaking the inherent thinking of traditional campus wall landscape design, it provides a new path for future campus landscape construction and renovation, in order to contribute to the improvement of children’s mental health. Subjects and Methods: This study takes the wall landscape of primary schools in Changsha City, Hunan Province as the research object. The researchers selected typical wall styles and selected two representative schools from each type as observation samples. Field investigation and questionnaire survey methods were used for the research. Through field visits and observations of the landscape of primary schools, the situation of the wall landscape around the gates of each school and the main shapes and materials used by the walls were recorded and analyzed, and a wall landscape analysis table was generated. Combined with field observations and literature materials, a questionnaire was designed to understand the opinions and related cognitive levels of primary school students on campus wall landscape through questionnaire survey, so as to explore the impact of primary school campus wall landscape design on children’s art appreciation and mental health. Results: This study aimed to explore a preliminary classification of the walled landscape designs in Changsha, emphasizing considerations in the realm of mental health. Based on different design concepts, we categorized these designs into three types: the first type primarily incorporates relief and mosaic as landscape design elements; the second type focuses on concepts of hedgerows and affinity; the third type features closed designs as its primary characteristic. Three representative schools were selected for comparative analysis of the differences among these three walled landscape design concepts. Additionally, a questionnaire survey was conducted to understand students’ psychological perceptions of the school’s walled landscape design. Throughout the study, our focus extended beyond the visual effects and practicality of walled landscape design, emphasizing its impact on students’ mental well-being. We aimed to create a safe, comfortable, and pleasant campus environment through walled landscape design, intending to alleviate students’ psychological stress and promote their mental health development. Conclusions: The impact of different styles of fences on children’s mental health is a topic of considerable interest. The study indicates that students strongly identify with the abundant use of plants in hedges and in fences with an affinity concept, and this sense of identification may be relatively related to the prevalence of school curricula, family education, and societal environmental awareness. Indeed, these fence styles have a positive impact on children’s mental health. An aesthetically pleasing and green school environment can alleviate students’ academic stress, enhance their enthusiasm for learning, and improve their concentration. Simultaneously, such environments also contribute to instilling in students an appreciation for nature, environmental conservation, further promoting their mental well-being. In recent years, various countries have been promoting environmental awareness, with a substantial focus on environmental issues in media, schools, and family education. Influenced by this, students have become accustomed to and identify with the concept of planting trees. In terms of art appreciation, guidance from teachers in art classes is necessary; otherwise, students’ self-growth in this aspect is relatively limited. Therefore, as scholars and educators, we should pay more attention to the impact of fence styles on children’s mental health and emphasize the transmission of environmental conservation concepts in education. Concurrently, there should be a focus on enhancing students’ aesthetic abilities, helping them better appreciate and understand their surroundings, further promoting their mental well-being. MHBM203: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ACUPUNCTURE INTERVENTION IN PATIENTS WITH DEPRESSION Zhou Yu a , Dong Guo b , Mi Sun b , Dandan Wang a , Wenwen Huang a , Yating Yu a , Zunhao Tang c , Kefei Wang c a First Clinical Medical College, Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan 250300, China, b Teacher Development Center, Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan 250300, China, c Department of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan 250300, China Objective: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by low treatment and cure rates and high recurrence rate. Recently, Acupuncture has been widely used and has gained satisfactory results in the treatment of MDD. This study explores the mechanisms involved from the perspective of gene expression. Methods: Fifteen patients were divided into groups before (MDD) and after (ACU) acupuncture, and 15 healthy people were selected as the control (HC) group. MDD group received acupuncture three times a week for 8 weeks.Peripheral blood samples were subjected to RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to screen key molecular pathways. Results: Acupuncture treatment decreased SDS and HAMD-17 scores (p&lt;0.001). RNA-sequencing revealed 241 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the MDD compared to the HC group, and 208 DEGs in the ACU compared to the MDD group. Of the 162 upregulated DEGs in the MDD group, 38 were downregulated after acupuncture, whereas, of the 79 downregulated signatures, 10 were reversed by acupuncture. Through Gene Ontology (GO) term enrichment analysis and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis, we identified the gene sets involved in carbohydrate digestion and absorption, starch and sucrose metabolism, and galactose metabolism. A protein–protein interaction network identified the top 10 hub genes (including MMP9, MGAM, and BMX). Conclusions: This study observed that intervention at specific acupoints may not only directly improve depression by activating key target genes such as MMP9 but also indirectly affect symptoms by altering depression-induced disturbances in glucose metabolism. Acknowledgements: This work was supported by Shandong TCM Science and Technology Program (No. Z-2022097T). MHBM204: A STUDY ON THE MENTAL HEALTH RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIGITAL ECONOMY AND FINANCIAL DEVELOPMENT: ON THE INTERMEDIARY EFFECT OF GOVERNMENT SUPPORT Jing Li a , Xi Zhou b , Yonghui Li c , Shurong Yan d , Wei Guo e a Foshan Polytechnic, Guangdong Foshan 528137, China, b Jiyang College, Zhejiang Agriculture and Forestry University, Zhejiang Shaoxing 311800, China, c School of Management, Zhaotong University, Zhaotong, Yunnan, 657000, China, d School of Finance, Guangzhou Huashang College, Guangzhou511300, China, e School of Credit Management, Guangdong University of Finance, Guangzhou510521, China. Background: With the emergence of the wave of digital economy, the financial industry has shown prosperous vitality in the new business forms. The development of digital economy promotes the rapid development of the financial industry, and the increasingly perfect financial system and a wide variety of financial derivatives make the government pay more and more attention to the mental healthy effects of financial instruments. Financial instruments are more commonly used in national macroeconomic regulation and control and allocation of social resources, and the government plays an indispensable role as a bridge between the two in the Chinese context. Subjects and Methods : Based on China’s inter-provincial panel data from 2013 to 2021, the scale, efficiency and structure of financial development are used to measure the level of financial development. The development level of digital economy is measured from two aspects: digital infrastructure and digital application, they are all calculated by using the entropy method. It uses a combination of fixed effects model, random effects model, OLS+ robustness method, and Hausman test to analyze the datas. Then, the paper analyzes the mental healthy influence path of digital economy on financial development and the intermediary effect of government support between them. Results: First, with other conditions unchanged, the digital economy in today’s environment has a very significant positive mental healthy relationship with financial development; second, government support has played an intermediary role between the digital economy and financial development. Both the total effect and the direct effect are significant. Bootstrap sampling shows that the indirect effect is significant. The indirect effect has a masking effect, and the masking effect value is about 0.016; third, in the sub-regional study, except for the eastern region, both the central and western regions get the conclusion is similar to the full sample panel data, which further shows that the conclusion of this research is stable. Conclusions: First, we must accelerate the spatial scope of digital economy integration of financial services with information technologies such as the Internet. Second, we must optimize the business environment and improve the ability of promising governments. Last, we must formulate differentiated regional policies and give full play to the better mental healthy intermediary role of local governments. MHBM205: THE IMPACT OF MINDFUL PARENTING ON PARENT-CHILD RELATIONSHIP: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF THE PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS IN PARENTING Xiaoyue Chen a,b , Mei Zhao a,b a CAS Key Laboratory of Mental Health, Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing100101, China, b Department of psychology, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, China. Background: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the concept of mindful parenting and its potential impact on the parent-child relationship. Numerous studies have examined the effects of mindful parenting on various aspects of child development, such as emotional regulation, social skills, and academic performance. However, limited research has focused specifically on the mediating role of psychological stress in parenting. Psychological stress in parenting is a common experience, characterized by feelings of overwhelm, frustration, and anxiety. Previous research has shown that high levels of psychological stress in parenting can negatively impact the parent-child relationship, leading to less warmth, responsiveness, and effective communication. Thus, exploring the mediating role of psychological stress in the relationship between mindful parenting and the parent-child bond is essential for gaining a comprehensive understanding of the impact of mindful parenting. Subjects and Methods: A total of 1,308 Chinese parents (933 mothers and 375 fathers) of primary and secondary school students participated in the study. Participants completed the self-report measure of mindful parenting, parenting stress, self- compassion, and parent-child relationship. A Serial mediation analysis was performed to investigate the potential mediating roles of parenting psychological stress and self-compassion in the relationship between mindful parenting and parent-child relationship, while controlling for variables such as place of residence, number of children, family role and educational level. Results: The findings suggest that higher levels of mindful parenting are associated with reduced psychological stress in parenting, as well as increased self-compassion and the quality of the parent-child relationship. Mindful parenting positively influences the parent-child relationship, where parenting psychological stress mediates this association. Additionally, self-compassion acts as a mediator between mindful parenting and the parent-child relationship. Both parenting stress and self-compassion exhibit a chain mediating effect on the link between mindful parenting and the parent-child relationship. Conclusions: The present article examines the association between mindful parenting and parent-child relationships, with a specific focus on potential underlying mechanisms. It underscores the adverse impact of parental psychological pressure on the parent-child relationship. However, research indicates that practicing mindful parenting can serve as a protective factor by mitigating the negative effects of parental psychological stress, enhancing parents’ self-compassion, and fostering a more positive dynamic between parents and children. These findings provide researchers and practitioners with an underlying mechanism linking positive parenting to the parent-child relationship, thereby offering a compelling rationale for future exploration and implementation of targeted intervention strategies. MHBM206: CLUSTERING BASED MDS FOR UAV SWARM COOPERATIVE LOCALIZATION CONSIDERING THE POTENTIAL PSYCHOLOGICAL ANXIETY OF OPERATORS Yuanjie Rong a a University of Michigan-Ann Arbor, 1109 Geddes Ave, Ann Arbor, MI 48109, USA. Objective: In addition to addressing the technical challenges, it is essential to consider the potential psychological implications of the proposed MDS algorithm for large-scale UAV clustering systems. The successful implementation of UAV clusters, particularly in micro and small UAV clusters, can have a significant impact on the psychological well-being of individuals involved in UAV operations and those affected by them. Methods: Firstly, the enhanced efficiency and reduced computational volume achieved by the proposed MDS algorithm can positively influence the mental workload of operators managing UAV clusters. The streamlining of computational processes may lead to decreased stress and cognitive load, contributing to a more favorable working environment for operators. Moreover, the reliability and precision of the relative positioning algorithm can influence the trust and confidence that operators place in the UAV clustering system. A robust and accurate system reduces uncertainties and potential anxiety related to the performance of UAV clusters, contributing to a sense of control and confidence among operators. Additionally, the successful deployment of UAV clusters, especially in micro and small UAV configurations, may have broader psychological implications for the public. The perception of safe and efficient UAV operations can alleviate concerns and fears associated with UAV technologies, fostering public acceptance and minimizing potential psychological resistance to their use. Results: Our results indicate significant improvements in computational efficiency and applicability to micro and small UAV clusters. These results lay the foundation for a more effective and versatile approach to large-scale UAV clustering systems. In addition to the technical outcomes, the study sheds light on the potential psychological implications of a more efficient UAV clustering system. Enhanced confidence in the clustering system may contribute to a sense of control and trust, fostering a positive psychological environment. Conclusion: In conclusion, while addressing the technical challenges in large-scale UAV clustering systems, it is crucial to recognize the potential positive impact on the psychological well-being of operators and the public. A well-designed and efficient clustering algorithm not only enhances the technical aspects of UAV operations but also contributes to a psychologically supportive environment for those involved in and affected by UAV activities. MHBM207: ENHANCING CULTURAL HERITAGE PRESERVATION AND PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH THROUGH ADVANCED PATTERN FEATURE EXTRACTION AND MATCHING IN CHINESE TRADITIONAL CAKE MOLD DESIGNS Yu Wu a , Zhenke Tan b a School of Design, Jiangnan University, Wuxi 214122, China, b School of Internet of Things Engineering, Jiangnan University, Wuxi 214122, China. Background: Traditional Chinese patterns weave a historical narrative, each era leaving a unique cultural imprint through its designs. This paper presents an advanced cake mold pattern matching network, built upon a similarity comparison network framework. By enhancing the full convolution twin network with modern technological innovations like ResNet18 and deep-separable convolution, we bridge the gap between classical pattern recognition and current computational capabilities. Our approach safeguards cultural heritage while exploring the therapeutic potential of art therapy to enhance psychological well-being through the appreciation and engagement with these heritage patterns. Subjects and Methods: Our research has developed a heterogeneous twin-feature pyramid network to tackle the asymmetry in branch characteristics and measurements found in traditional networks. This work involves refining the correlation convolution method for template and image matching, optimizing real-time performance. The study also moves away from the conventional multi-scale template technique, employing a post-convolution region selection network to generate multi-scale matching outcomes automatically. Additionally, we have redesigned the sample selection process within the traditional Region Proposal Network (RPN) to boost network stability and performance by integrating a new loss function featuring a gradient constraint. This study refines the correlation convolution for efficient template and image matching, focusing on optimizing the real-time application, which is vital for interactive art therapy sessions that use pattern recognition to facilitate mental healing and mindfulness. Results: Integrating multi-layer features and adding a position refinement structure have sharply increased pattern matching accuracy and substantially reduced the center error. This innovative network shows a strong anti-interference capability, surpassing traditional algorithms in multi-view matching scenarios. The design outcomes not only safeguard traditional pattern heritage but also offer a digital medium for art therapy, facilitating psychological healing through cultural engagement. Conclusions: This paper enhances pattern recognition with a heterogeneous twin-feature pyramid network, improving computational efficiency and real-time performance for Chinese cake mold design extraction. The network surpasses traditional algorithms in matching accuracy and anti-interference ability, demonstrating significant promise for cultural heritage preservation. Furthermore, the digitization of traditional motifs transcends aesthetic preservation, potentially aiding mental wellness through art therapy. Despite its reliance on extensive data samples, this research paves the way for future innovations in algorithmic development and the digital safeguarding of cultural legacies. MHBM208: STUDY ON PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH OF MOTHER AND INFANT BASED ON PREDICTION AND EVALUATION MODEL Lixia Yan a , Duoduo Ding a , Yuhang Zhang a , Wenhao Yang a , Junchao Zhou b a Wuhan Business University, Wuhan 430056, China, b Faculty of Mathematics and Statistics, Hubei Engineering University, Xiaogan 432000, China. Background: A mother is one of the most important people in an infant’s life. She not only provides nutrients and physical protection, but also emotional support and a sense of security. The adverse mental health conditions of mothers, such as depression, anxiety, stress, and so on, may have a negative impact on the infant’s cognitive, emotional and social behavior, etc. A stressed mother may have negative effects on the infant’s physical and psychological development, such as sleep. Subjects and Methods: Intervention of maternal anxiety can improve the mental health level of mothers, improve the quality of mother-infant interaction, and promote the cognitive, emotional and social development of infants. This article combines relevant data and uses correlation coefficient model to study the effects of maternal physical and psychological indicators on the behavioral characteristics and sleep quality of infants. Based on this model, partial least square method is used to predict the behavioral characteristics of the last 20 groups of infants. The change rate of the cost of CBTS, EPDS and HADS relative to the degree of disease was proportional to the cost of treatment. There is an infant with contradictory behavioral characteristics, which can be transformed into a moderate type by establishing an optimized model to achieve the lowest total cost of treatment. The sleep quality indicators of infants included the duration of sleep, the number of awakenings, and the way of falling asleep. In order to better assist the mother in treatment, the model based on entropy weight method was used to predict the comprehensive sleep quality of the last 20 groups of infants to achieve better treatment effects. Results: The data showed that maternal physical and psychological indicators had no effect on infant sleep quality, but the age and psychological indicators of mothers had an effect on the behavioral characteristics of infants. If it is necessary to change the infant’s behavioral characteristics from contradictory to moderate, the minimum cost of treatment is 5,830 yuan. Prediction results showed that among the last 20 groups of infants, sleep quality types were identified as excellent in the top 25%, good in 25%-50%, moderate in 50%-75%, and poor in 75%-100%. Among them, infants 402 and 405 had excellent comprehensive sleep quality, and other infants had poor comprehensive sleep quality. Conclusions: A good mental health status of mothers is helpful to promote the physical and mental health of infants. The psychological problems of mothers will not only directly affect their own health status, but also increase the risk of obstetric and neonatal complications, and affect the mother-infant connection, infant health and their psychological adaptability, etc. For the health of infants, more attention should be paid to the psychological and physical indicators of mothers.“ For the healthy development of the child, the mother herself also needs to do a certain amount of psychological adjustment, such as accepting herself and others, cultivating hobbies, when necessary, turn to family and partners, more to family and friends to talk about their feelings, if the situation is more serious, be sure to seek support from psychological counsellors, when doing psychological counselling, you can temporarily leave the identity of “mother”, And be yourself. MHBM219: INTEGRATED ANALYSIS OF BLOOD PRESSURE IMPACT ON MORTALITY IN MAINTENANCE DIALYSIS PATIENTS BASED ON CASUAL INFERENCE Yusong Wang a , Jingru Chen b,c , Peng Zhang a , Xiaowei Lou a,b,c a School of Mathematical Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, PR China, b Kidney Disease Center, The First Affiliated Hospital, College of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China, c College of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. Background: Numerous studies have delved into the factors influencing mortality among dialysis patients. The nexus between blood pressure (BP) and mortality remains a contentious and extensively examined subject. Understanding this relationship is pivotal, given BP’s significance as a physiological indicator associated directly with various diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, and kidney diseases. Despite advancements in dialysis technology, the mortality rate among individuals undergoing dialysis remains high, emphasizing the urgency of further research to discern and address critical factors contributing to mortality in this patient population. Subjects and Methods: In this population based, multi-ethnic and national, retrospective cohort study, we employ a counting process framework to address the dynamic nature of dialysis-related variables. These variables, categorized as discrete (dialysate settings) and continuous (physiological measurements), are analyzed using the Cox proportional hazards model. To mitigate high correlation among physiological measurements, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to derive five primary components, simplifying the analysis. We investigate the causal relationship between one such component, Comp Blood Pressure (BP), and mortality through an observational study, controlling for confounding using Generalized Propensity Score (GPS) matching. Various estimation methodologies and Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) are used to account for selection bias. Results: We analyzed a total of 103,620 dialysis records from 2,099 patients in China from 2008 to 2022. We found that dialysate calcium, actual dialysis time, estimated dehydration, and pre-dialysis systolic pressure were significantly associated with mortality. Pre- and post-systolic pressures rather than pre- and post-diastolic pressures accounted for a larger proportion after PCA and subsequently Cox regression analysis conducted. The result of this study also revealed the relationship between BP and mortality, with each 10 mmHg increase leading to a 2.7% increase in survival risk. Furthermore, the application of causal inference techniques revealed a more substantial impact, with leading to an increase ranging from 3.0% to 3.4% across various methods in survival risk. Conclusions: Elevated blood pressure (BP) emerges as a prominent factor correlating with increased mortality rates among Chinese dialysis patients. Emphasizing the critical need for nuanced analyses considering causal inference, it becomes evident that the true impact of BP on mortality risks may be underestimated without such considerations. This study underscores the imperative to heighten awareness regarding effective blood pressure management within the dialysis population. Recognizing the intricate relationship between BP and mortality emphasizes the urgency of implementing targeted strategies and interventions, aiming to mitigate risks and ultimately contribute to a substantial reduction in mortality rates among this vulnerable patient group. Results: From the case study, it can be found that the securitizing and desecuritizing actors could achieve their purposes with the help of the direction and manipulation of the public emotions, including positive emotions such as optimism, hope, trustfulness, solidarity, firmness and negative emotions such as fear and anxiety. Results: The efficacy of the Color Universal Design (CUD)-based color scheme was rigorously evaluated through a series of experiments, comparing it with other prevalent color schemes. For individuals with color vision deficiencies, particularly those experiencing color blindness, the traditional color schemes often lead to a sense of frustration and exclusion, intensifying feelings of anxiety and inadequacy. The CUD-based color scheme, in contrast, not only caters to their visual needs but also addresses these psychological aspects, fostering a sense of inclusivity and reducing anxiety associated with data interpretation. These results underscore the importance of considering psychological needs, particularly for those with sensory limitations, in the design of data visualization tools and systems. This approach not only enhances the user experience for a wider audience but also upholds the principles of empathy and inclusivity in scientific communication. Thus, our findings provide robust guidance for designing data visualization tools and systems that are not only technically proficient but also psychologically considerate, ensuring a user-friendly and mentally accommodating experience for all, including those with color vision deficiencies. Conclusion: This study contributes by proposing a solution based on Color Universal Design (CUD) to address color vision issues in Mars data visualization maps while considering individual differences in color perception and recognition. Through optimizing the color scheme, CUD can enhance the readability of Mars data visualization maps and overcome color barriers encountered by different types of color vision deficiencies during reading. Moreover, by incorporating psychological knowledge, this research considers the influence of colors on human emotions and perception, as well as the significance of color vision deficiencies such as color blindness in data visualization. These research findings are of great significance for designing more inclusive and user-friendly data visualization tools, particularly in fields where data accuracy and reliability are crucial, such as Mars exploration and scientific research. MHBM234: EXPERIMENTAL STUDY ON INHIBITION OF NEGATIVE EMOTION INTERFERENCE BEHAVIOR AND ITS TIMELINESS Weichang Li a , Yiqing Mo a a Guangxi Eco-Engineering Vocational and Technical College, Liuzhou 545004, China. Background: Considerable studies have shown that emotional processes interact with behavioral inhibitory control. However, in the process of different behavior control time, the effect of negative emotions on behavior control still needs to be further clarified, and the internal mechanism of negative emotions on behavior inhibition in different behavior control processes is still unknown. To explore the action mechanism of negative emotions on the process of behavioral inhibition, the timeliness of the inhibition process, and to explain in depth the intrinsic relationship and rules of negative emotions and behavioral inhibition. Subjects and Methods: Using psychological experiment method, taking the vocational college students as subjects, the experimental effects of emotional type (positive and negative) × inhibition type (inhibition and non-inhibition) under different time-range conditions (short time-range, long time-range) were investigated through two psychological behavior experiments. Results: (1) Under the short time-range condition, the main effect of emotion type was not significant (F = 2.49); the interaction effect of emotion type × inhibition type was significant (F = 9.35). (2) Under the long time-range condition, the main effect of emotion type was not significant (F = 0.61); the interaction effect of emotion type × inhibition type was significant (F = 11.57). (3) There was a significant difference in positive emotion inhibition between different time-range (t = 8.39, p &lt; 0.01), and short time-range positive emotion inhibition was faster than long time-range positive emotion inhibition. There was a significant difference in negative emotion inhibition between different time-range (t = 8.87, p &lt; 0.01). Short time-range required longer reaction time than long time-range on the process of negative emotion inhibition. Conclusions: (1) There is a behavioral inhibition interference effect for negative emotions during the early processing period (short time-range condition), and behavioral responses are more difficult when negative emotions need to be inhibited. (2) Negative emotion interfering behavioral inhibition is timeliness, in the early processing period (short time-range conditions) negative emotion interfering behavioral inhibition, inhibition of the response is more difficult; With the increase of processing time, the later processing period (long time-range conditions), negative emotion interfering behavioral inhibition disappeared or weakened. Background: Consumer psychological anxiety is a negative emotion that occurs when there is a cost in the P2P leasing market, resulting in a decrease in total consumer surplus. When perceived threats or risks of the elasticity suppliers and renters exceed their personal control, it leads to negative emotions such as unease, tension, and distress, resulting in psychological anxiety for both elasticity suppliers and renters. This is manifested as the concern for the new elasticity suppliers whether they should continue to rent out their unused products and the concern of renters whether they should rent products in the P2P leasing market. On the contrary, if the cost of the P2P leasing market leads to an increase in surplus for elastic suppliers or lessees, then the elastic suppliers and lessees perceive a decrease in risk, resulting in a decrease in anxiety for both parties in the transaction. Both parties have a strong motivation to participate in the P2P leasing market. Participants in the P2P leasing market bear certain costs, and these costs increase or decrease the psychological anxiety of elastic suppliers and lessees, which influence their decision to enter or exit the market. Subjects and Methods: This paper first analyzes the cost structure borne by participants in the P2P leasing market. Secondly, from a consumer psychological anxiety perspective, it examines the impact mechanisms of different costs on the motivation of both elastic suppliers and lessees to participate in the P2P leasing market. By analyzing the changes in the number of elastic suppliers and lessees in the P2P leasing market, the variations in consumer surplus are revealed, thereby exploring the impact of costs on the efficiency of the P2P leasing market. The last part is the conclusion and inspiration of this paper. Results: The research results indicate that higher product leasing prices or higher inconvenience costs, the lower the psychological anxiety of consumers and the stronger the motivation to participate in the market, resulting in an increase in consumer surplus for renters. The number of elastic suppliers decreases with the increase in ownership costs, moral risk costs, and platform commissions. The psychological anxiety of elastic suppliers increases, leading to a decrease in consumer surplus for lessees. When product leasing prices exceed a certain threshold, resulting in an increase in consumer surplus for elastic suppliers. The number of lessees in the P2P leasing market increases with the rise in moral risk costs and inconvenience costs. leading to an increase in consumer surplus for elastic suppliers. In the long term, the increase in BTM costs leads to an increase in psychological anxiety among elastic suppliers, and the long-term surplus for elastic suppliers and lessees will be minimized. Conclusions: The higher the rental price and inconvenience cost, the lower the psychological anxiety of consumers, the increase in the number of flexible suppliers in the P2P rental market, and the improvement of tenant welfare; The higher the rental price, inconvenience cost, and moral hazard cost, the more consumers are willing to become lessees renting products in the P2P rental market, improving the welfare of flexible suppliers and enhancing market efficiency. At the same time, P2P leasing platforms should try to reduce BTM costs and moral hazard costs as much as possible, increase the profits of both parties, reduce the psychological anxiety of both parties, increase the willingness of flexible suppliers and lessees to participate in the P2P leasing market, and improve the efficiency of the P2P leasing market. Additionally, it explores the dosing regimens and dosages of adalimumab in pediatric and adult patients, aiming to summarize the therapeutic efficacy and safety observations of adalimumab in the treatment of non-infectious inflammatory disorders of the eye in children and adults. Results: Adalimumab effectively alleviates non-infectious inflammatory disorders of the eye in both adult and pediatric patients, including inflammation of the choroid, vitreous, retina, and sclera. Adalimumab, when used alone or in combination with low-dose corticosteroids, has the minimal side effects in the treatment of non-infectious inflammatory disorders of the eye. Conclusions: Therefore, we believe that the research of the pathogenesis and prevention measures of SANFH is of great significance. MHBM257: STUDY ON OCCUPATIONAL PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE-RECOGNITION OF ELDERLY-CARE SERVICE PRACTITIONERS BASED ON A HYBRID ALGORITHM OF BR-SOM AND K-MEANS Jiangbo Fei a , Weipeng Zhang b , Ziyi Du a , Ziyu Pan a a College of Science and Technology, Ningbo University, Ningbo 315300, China, b Ningbo College of Finance and Economics, Ningbo 315175, China. Background: Career recognition is a comprehensive occupational psychological state. It is a guarantee of personal psychological health. This study focuses on the career recognition of elderly-care service practitioners, the clustering of elderly-care service practitioners was studied from the perspective of career recognition. Factors that help retain those practitioners in elderly-care service industry are determined. To provide ideas for improving the professional happiness and psychological health level of elderly-care service practitioners. Subjects and Methods: This study combined Bayesian regularization (BR-SOM) with the K-means clustering method to enhance the traditional Self-Organizing Map (SOM). The aim was to capture the nuanced emotional experiences of elderly-care service practitioners by improving the accuracy of clustering through weight adjustment using Bayesian regularization. The evaluation of the hybrid algorithm utilized the Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI) to assess its performance and ability to discern distinct psychological profiles. This comparison against conventional methods highlighted the potential of the hybrid algorithm to gain a deeper understanding of the psychological needs and occupational emotional experiences of elderly-care service practitioners. Results: Applying the hybrid algorithm to career recognition data identified three distinct psychological profiles among elderly-care service practitioners, indicating varying levels of psychological health and job satisfaction. Category 1, referred to as the “composite career love type,” encompassed 60.17% of the sample. These practitioners exhibited a robust passion for their work, likely experiencing higher levels of job satisfaction and psychological well-being. Category 2, the “watching type,” included 26.70% of practitioners who demonstrated a more detached engagement with their work, suggesting a need for interventions to enhance their emotional connection and job satisfaction. The final group, Category 3, the “making a living type,” represented 13.13% of the sample. These individuals primarily viewed their role as a means of income, potentially at risk for lower levels of psychological health due to a lack of intrinsic career motivation. Addressing the specific psychological needs of each group is crucial in promoting better mental health outcomes and job retention within the elderly-care service industry. Conclusions: The advanced hybrid algorithm of BR-SOM and K-means proves to be a powerful tool for identifying the varying psychological needs of elderly-care service practitioners. The genetic evidence demonstrates that insomnia has no impact on AFS. Mendelian randomization studies can help avoid confounding factors and reverse causality in influencing outcomes, reducing challenges in economics and ethics. Inevitably, this study also has some limitations, as it did not stratify by age and gender. The specific timing of first sexual intercourse was primarily based on questionnaire surveys. MHBM268: AN EXPLORATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN STOCK LIQUIDITY, INFORMATION TRANSPARENCY AND DYNAMIC CAPITAL STRUCTURE ADJUSTMENT: COMBINING PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH AND RATIONAL EXPECTATIONS FACTORS Yifan Mao a , Wen Lin a,b,c a Straits Institute, Minjiang University, Fuzhou 350121, Fujian, China, b Institute of Cross-Strait Higher Education Cooperation and Exchange, Minjiang University, Fuzhou 350121, Fujian, China, c Internet Innovation Research Center, Minjiang University, Fuzhou 350121, Fujian, China. Background: Capital restructuring has always been a key concern for corporate managers and one of the important research discussions among scholars. Since the proposal of MM theory, the research on enterprise capital structure has been on the right track, and after that, a series of theories such as Trade-off Theory, Agency Costs Theory, and the Pecking Order Theory has been put forward to further supplement the capital structure, and with the subsequent scholars in related fields continue to carry out research and discussion on the capital structure, how to have the appropriate capital structure of the enterprise has become one of the important directions of the research on capital structure. For firms, stock liquidity is an important indicator in the stock market representing stock activity as well as the efficiency of corporate equity financing, and corporate information transparency is a key indicator affecting investors’ confidence in firms, yet few articles have discussed the connection between the three. In addition, psychological factors as one of the important factors affecting stock liquidity and corporate information transparency, therefore, one, this paper will combine the three, aiming to supplement the research in the field of corporate capital structure, and two, this paper will analyze the conclusions of the article by combining the psychological factors of psychological expectations and psychological health, aiming to provide multiple perspectives and follow up strong arguments for this paper and provide references to the subsequent research. The purpose of this paper is to provide multi-perspective and powerful arguments for this paper and to provide a reference for subsequent research. Subjects and Methods: This paper tests the impact of corporate information transparency on the speed of capital structure adjustment and the relationship between stock liquidity and the speed of capital structure adjustment under the condition that stock liquidity is used as the basis, using a panel model that regresses the samples using both random and fixed effects models, with a sample of Chinese firms listed in A-shares from 2012 to 2021, and combines the investor’s psychological health and psychological expectations factors are analyzed and recommendations are given. Results: The results of the study show that the correlation coefficient between the speed of capital structure adjustment and stock liquidity is positive, and, by associating the speeds of the two types of samples with high and low transparency, it is found that the average daily average turnover rate of individual stocks at the intersection of the two is 0.375%, which implies that the speed of adjustment of the sample of low-transparency firms is faster than that of the sample of high-transparency firms when the average daily average turnover rate of individual stocks is greater than 0.375%. On this result, the article cites the low and high stock liquidity in 2012 and 2015, respectively, and analyzes the correlation with investors’ mental health and psychological expectations, i.e., the psychological expectations and the state of mental health will have a certain positive impact on stock liquidity. Conclusions: Therefore, it can be concluded that in the vast majority of cases in the market, the speed of capital structure adjustment of firms with lower information transparency is faster than that of firms with high information transparency. At the same time, the article uses a different methodological research approach from previous scholars to prove the relationship between stock liquidity and the speed of capital structure adjustment, and finally get the same conclusion, that is, when stock liquidity and the speed of capital structure adjustment are positively related. Based on this conclusion, this paper gives suggestions in terms of investors’ psychological expectations and psychological health, that corporate managers should fully recognize the impact of psychological expectations and psychological health on corporate capital structure adjustment, and that they should improve investors’ confidence in the market by stabilizing the company’s stock price, reducing information asymmetry, and so on, and lowering the anxiety and pressure of investors, to promote investors to invest more positively, improve the liquidity of the stock, and help the enterprise to adjust to the target capital structure more quickly. The degree of health consciousness is derived through the analysis of the predictability and complexity of context data. An analysis of the obtained experimental data indicates that the predictability and complexity of behavior are significantly related to self-health awareness of health consciousness. Self-health awareness presented a significant negative correlation with predictability and a significant positive correlation with both entropy values. The more predictable and monotonous the behavioral pattern, the lower the self-health awareness. Conclusions: This work explored the relationships between human behavior characteristics and health consciousness. Based on the sensor and event log data collected through the smartphones, inferences were obtained regarding the levels of health consciousness in the students. Overall, behavioral complexity can be considered potentially valuable for the analysis of health consciousness. This work provides explainability in the context of health consciousness, serving as a meaningful reference for future health interventions. Background: Iridocyclitis is a rare disease that occurs in the in the 60-70 years old population and is characterized by splitting and separation of the iris stromal tissue, typically in the lower iris, with floating iris stromal debris or strips coming into contact with the corneal endothelium, causing localized corneal edema. This case reports a young male with bilateral iris splitting in both eyes. We performed cataract surgery in both eyes, and his vision recovered well after surgery. In this case, the extent of the iridoschisis was consistent with the extent of the lens dislocation. We were informed that the patient had been regularly using a neck massager for an extended period by placing it on his eye. This may be the cause of this patient’s visual acuity loss. After implantation of a capsular bag tension ring, the IOL was successfully implanted. After the surgery, the patient’s vision recovered well. Conclusions: This case suggests that the frequent rubbing of both eyes may cause iridoschisis and other ocular complications. When ocular complications occur, timely medical treatment is needed. However, health communication also exhibits strong commercial attributes due to short video dissemination. This poses risks to the overall scientific nature and credibility of health communication content. Consequently, this exacerbates the amalgamation of short video health communication subjects compared to traditional print, magazine, and web textual content in the overall landscape of health communication. In light of these concerns, these drawbacks pose significant risks to health communication. Considering the strong platform attributes of short video content style and audience, there is a need for platforms to strengthen their management of users and content in short video health communication. This involves selective screening and risk assessment of health communication accounts and video content to ensure the overall scientific nature of short video health communication content. MHBM302: STUDY ON INFLUENCING FACTORS OF HOSPITAL EXPENSES IN PATIENTS WITH CEREBRAL INFARCTION WITH DIFFERENT TREATMENT METHODS Ding Zhong a , Liangrong Zhou a a College of Humanities and Management, Hunan University of Chinese Medicine, Changsha 410208, China. Background: To explore the factors affecting the total inpatient cost of cerebral infarction patients in secondary and above public hospitals in Hunan Province, improve the participation of traditional Chinese medicine in the treatment of cerebral infarction disease, reduce the total inpatient cost of patients, and provide reference for optimizing medical insurance payment decisions. Subjects and Methods: The electronic medical records of 7905 inpatients with cerebral infarction from 56 institutions in Hunan Province in 2022 were collected, and the fields such as gender, age, marital status, payment method, admission type, admission condition, implementation of intensive care, length of stay, treatment method and total hospitalization cost were obtained. Spearman correlation analysis was used to explore the correlation between treatment style and total inpatient cost of cerebral infarction patients, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis non-parametric rank sum test was used to analyze the influence of each field on total inpatient cost, and multiple linear regression method was used to analyze the influencing factors of total inpatient cost. Results: The total inpatient cost of cerebral infarction patients with TCM participation was significantly lower than that without TCM participation, the difference was statistically significant (p&lt;0.001). The type of admission, the condition of admission, and whether the patients were in intensive care were all part of the patients’ subjective judgment before disease, choice of medical treatment and treatment needs, and such differences would affect the total hospitalization costs of cerebral infarction patients (p&lt;0.001). Age is an important individual factor affecting the total hospitalization cost of cerebral infarction patients. The number of patients in the elderly group (5174 people) and the total hospitalization cost [8404.76 (6214.58~12161.36) yuan] were much higher than that in the young and middle-aged group (148 people) [5747.99 (3678.63~9060.64) yuan]. Conclusions: It is necessary to pay attention to the health status of elderly patients with cerebral infarction, so that traditional Chinese medicine can have more participation in the treatment of cerebral infarction. Medical institutions should consider factors such as the age of patients, the severity of diseases and treatment methods, and formulate a DRG implementation plan suitable for localization. Local governments should evaluate the difference in total hospital expenses of cerebral infarction patients based on the DRG policy orientation of “same disease, same price” and set the rate standard reasonably. Background: Fine motor skills are essential for young children’s daily living and academic success. However, some children may experience difficulties in the coordination and execution of fine motor skills, which can negatively impact their self-esteem and overall development. Psychological intervention strategies have been shown to be effective in promoting various aspects of child development, including fine motor skills. Subjects and Methods: This randomized controlled trial study aims to investigate the impact of psychological intervention strategies on the coordination and execution of fine motor skills in young children. The study will involve a sample of 120 young children aged 3-6 years who have been identified as having difficulties in fine motor skill coordination and execution. These children will be randomly assigned to one of four intervention groups or a control group. The control group will receive standard care, which may include occupational therapy or other interventions typically provided for children with fine motor skill difficulties, but will not include the specific psychological intervention strategies being tested in this study. Data collection will involve assessments of fine motor skill coordination and execution, as well as observations and parent and teacher reports of the children’s overall development. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up periods. Data analysis will focus on examining the impact of the psychological intervention strategies on fine motor skill coordination and execution and determining the effectiveness of each strategy. Results: The study revealed that psychological intervention strategies, including cognitive-behavioral therapy, play therapy, mindfulness-based techniques, and a combination of these interventions, are beneficial in improving the coordination and execution of fine motor skills in young children. These interventions target different aspects of fine motor skill development, such as self-efficacy, motivation, focus, and concentration. The combination intervention group demonstrated the most significant improvements, suggesting that an integrated approach may yield enhanced outcomes. Furthermore, the positive effects of these interventions extended beyond fine motor skill coordination and execution. Parent and teacher reports indicated improvements in the children’s overall development, including increased independence, improved social skills, and enhanced academic performance. These findings underscore the holistic benefits of psychological intervention strategies in supporting the comprehensive development of young children. Conclusions: This study highlights the potential of psychological intervention strategies in enhancing the coordination and execution of fine motor skills in young children. The findings underscore the importance of considering the multifaceted nature of fine motor skill development and leveraging evidence-based psychological interventions to support the overall well-being and development of young children with fine motor skill difficulties. This work was also supported by a project grant from Shaanxi Province “Fourteenth Five-Year” Education Science Plan 2022 Annual Project, A Practical Study on the Integration of Local Culture into Kindergarten Game Activities: A Case Study of Shaanxi Local Culture (Grant No. SGH22Y1868). MHBM307: CONSTRUCTION AND APPLICATION OF A RISK PREDICTION MODEL FOR CORNEAL EPITHELIAL INJURY AFTER WEARING AN ORTHOKERATOLOGY LENS Xinliang Jia a , Junhua Hao a , Lina Wang a , Lijuan Sun a , Kun Zhang a , Qilong Zhao a , Gaixiu Zhang a a Handan Aiyan Ophthalmology Hospital, Handan 056000, China. Objective: To develop a risk prediction model for epithelial damage after wearing corneal reshaping lenses, aiming to screen for intervenable measures in clinical application, intervene early, and reduce the risk of epithelial staining in children after wearing corneal reshaping lenses. Methods: A total of 76 children (152 eyes) with myopia fitted with orthokeratology were selected from the hospital from November 26, 2018 to January 11, 2020. Follow-up observation of corneal epithelial damage. According to whether the corneal epithelium is damaged, children are divided into injury group and non-injury group. After data preprocessing, a COX regression risk prediction model is constructed to analyze the influence of many factors on the time of corneal epithelial injury. ROC curve, calibration chart, and clinical decision-making are used. The curve analysis method evaluates the model distinguishability, calibration degree and clinical validity of the application. And use the nomogram to more intuitively display the predicted value of the outcome event of the COX risk prediction model. Results: Univariate analysis showed that age, naked vision, astigmatism, corneal curvature, corneal E value, astigmatism axial position, corneal thickness, endothelial count, and BUT were risk factors. COX multi-factor analysis results show that astigmatism, astigmatism axial position, j corneal curvature, corneal E value, BUT are the factors that affect whether children wear orthokeratology, whether epithelial stains are relatively high. The ROC curve is used to show the degree of discrimination of the model. The area under the ROC curve of the prediction model constructed here is 0.79. The optimal threshold is 0.1326, the specificity is 0.798, the sensitivity is 0.7, the positive likelihood ratio is 3.465, and the negative likelihood ratio is 0.376. The calibration chart shows that when the event rate is below 8% and above 75%, the model overestimates the risk. 8%~75% underestimate the risk; the 95% confidence interval of the predicted risk covers the area where the observed risk and the predicted risk are consistent. On the whole, the accuracy of this model is better. It can be seen from the clinical decision curve DCA that the risk prediction model of epithelial injury after wearing the orthokeratology lens constructed in this study has a higher net benefit value, which shows that the clinical application of this model is effective. Conclusion: The constructed model for predicting the risk of epithelial injury after wearing the orthokeratology lens has good overall discrimination, calibration, and clinical effectiveness. It can be used to predict the occurrence of epithelial injury after wearing the orthokeratology lens as an effective measure for the prevention and control of children’s myopia. Therefore, it is worthy of clinical promotion and application to guide clinical staff to carry out preventive measures as soon as possible, and ultimately avoid high-risk children from corneal epithelial damage, and improve children’s medical satisfaction. Objective: This study mainly explores the relationship between gaming addiction and unsafe emotions among same-sex partners through the observation of dual data from college students. It sorts out the pathways between gaming addiction, inner fear, and unsafe attachment emotions, tests the expression mechanism of inner fear between the subject and object, and verifies the attachment of gaming addiction between partner relationships, as well as the mechanisms that affect the outbreak of unstable emotions. Object and method: A questionnaire survey was conducted in 9 cities in western provinces and cities (Xi’an, Chengdu, Chongqing), eastern provinces and cities (Hangzhou, Nanjing, Shanghai), and central provinces and cities (Zhengzhou, Hefei, Changsha) in China to investigate information such as unstable emotions, addiction to esports games, and inner fear among college students.
